 This is a part-time, remote role for a hands-on engineer who can build, ship and lead. You will own delivery across a Flutter mobile app and a React-based web console. You will guide a small team of developers who work across both frameworks. You will also write production code yourself.
 You will wear several hats:
 Developer: build screens, APIs and data flows across mobile, web and backend.

 Build and maintain a cross-platform mobile app in Flutter/Dart (state management, navigation, offline caching, push notifications via FCM/APNs, deep links, app-store releases).

 Model data in PostgreSQL (Supabase). This includes schema design, migrations, indexing, time-partitioned tables, JSONB columns, views, and Row-Level Security (RLS) policies for multi-tenant data isolation.
 Implement authentication and authorisation: JWT/OAuth2, role-based access control (RBAC) , MFA, and audit logging.
 Build real-time features with WebSockets, Server-Sent Events or database change subscriptions , with throttled live updates and graceful handling of stale or missing data.

 Run DevOps : Docker, Railway deployments, GitHub Actions CI/CD, environment and secret management, TLS, logging, metrics and alerting (Prometheus/Grafana, Sentry), and release management.

 Backend experience with Python (FastAPI) or Node.js . You should understand async programming, REST design and API versioning.

 Hands-on experience with Docker and CI/CD pipelines, and with deploying to a cloud or PaaS platform.
 Knowledge of Protobuf, GraphQL, Next.js SSR/SSG, PWA, Capacitor, or React Native.
 Familiarity with authentication and security basics: JWT, OAuth2, CORS, CSRF/XSS and secrets handling.
 Experience integrating third-party and external APIs: webhook handling, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, rate limiting, and idempotent writes (for example, payment gateways, weather APIs, push services).
 Familiarity with the medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture on S3-compatible object storage. This includes Parquet/Apache Iceberg tables, dbt transformations, Airflow scheduling, and querying with DuckDB or Polars.
 Clear written and spoken communication, including the ability to explain technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders and executives.

 Redis, RabbitMQ, Celery/Arq, or background-job patterns.
 Data visualisation (Chart.js, ECharts, D3, Recharts, canvas/WebGL) and dashboard UX.

 Monorepo tooling, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, and observability (OpenTelemetry, Grafana).
 LLM/RAG exposure: embeddings, vector search, prompt grounding and evaluation.
 Interest in energy, utilities, IoT, smart meters or hardware-connected software.
 Prior experience mentoring juniors or leading a small project.

 Part-time and remote. You set your own hours inside an agreed weekly schedule, with a few overlap hours for stand-ups and reviews.

 Experience in EdTech or building products for students.

About Sarvam 
 Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC and LIC.
About the role 
 Sarvam's model APIs (ASR, TTS, Vision, LLM, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. The platform handles tens of millions of API calls every day, over HTTP and WebSockets, with metering, billing, prepaid wallets and rate-limiting all part of the same stack.
 We are hiring a Software Engineer to own major parts of this platform end to end, working closely with the Staff Engineer who leads its architecture. You will take an area such as speech to text pipeline,or text to speech pipeline, and be accountable for its reliability, performance and end-to-end latencies. This role is for someone who is obsessed with latencies, optimizes services and network paths to shave off milliseconds, ships fast, reasons from first principles, and treats AI as the default way to get engineering work done.
What you will do 
Own a platform area end to end 
 • Own one or more major parts of the platform, such as the WebSocket streaming layer, a speech recognition pipeline, or text to speech pipeline: build, operate and improve them.
 • Turn loosely defined goals into RFCs, milestones and shipped results, and write down the decisions and trade-offs.
 • Be accountable after launch: on-call, incident response, root-cause analysis and follow-through on fixes.
 • Make the call when a decision is needed, and own the outcome.
 • Obsessed with latencies, dissecting existing services to understand the system, and tuning the right knobs to optimize performance.
 • Bring services across without regressions in customer-facing APIs, latency or reliability.
Build real-time and model-serving pipelines 
 • Build and operate streaming infrastructure: WebSocket connections, long-lived sessions queue-based batch processing, backpressure and low-latency model invocation.
 • Engineer audio pipelines: TTS chunking around model context limits, sample-rate conversion and format encoding, and VAD-based silence detection for ASR.
 • Hold your services to sub-100ms latency SLOs in a multi-tenant environment, and know where every millisecond goes.
Think in systems and from first principles 
 • Reasons from constraints: latency budgets per hop, throughput, cost per request, failure modes and tenant isolation.
 • Use back-of-the-envelope estimates to decide what to build, what to optimize and what to leave alone.
 • Prefer simple designs you can fully explain over clever ones you cannot.
 • Build in observability from day one: logging, metrics and tracing that let anyone debug production quickly.
Raise the bar for the team 
 • Strengthen the integration testing harness so the team can ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs.
 • Partner with the Inference and MLOps teams on making model serving fast, reliable and operable.
 • Mentor junior engineers through RFC reviews, code review and pairing.
 • Practice design-first, documentation-first engineering: RFCs before code, no tribal knowledge.
What we are looking for 
 • 4–6 years of building and operating production backend systems.
 • At least one service you owned end to end under real load, including what broke and what you changed.
 • Strong distributed-systems fundamentals: concurrency, networking, queues, caching, consistency and failure modes.
 • Experience with low-latency or high-throughput services, and comfort reasoning about p95 and p99 latency.
 • Solid fundamentals with a relational database and a cache, such as PostgreSQL and Redis: schema design, query performance and caching strategy.
 • Fluency in at least one backend language and willingness to work in both Python and Golang.
 • Experience running services with containers, CI/CD and production monitoring.
 • Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in your engineering workflow, with concrete examples of what you automated or sped up.
 • A bias for action: fast on reversible decisions, careful on irreversible ones.
 • Clear writing, especially RFCs and design docs that others can act on.
Good to have (not required) 
 • Voice AI or real-time audio experience: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming ASR or TTS, or audio processing with FFmpeg or pyav, codecs, sample rates and VAD.
 • Production experience in Go, or in Python with FastAPI.
 • Experience serving LLM, ASR, TTS or vision models in production.
 • Experience building metering, billing, wallet or payments infrastructure.
 • Running services on Kubernetes in production.
 • Time at an early- or growth-stage startup.
Why Sarvam 
 • A fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, with real population-scale impact.
 • Researchers, engineers, builders and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar.
 • High ownership and high impact from day one.
 • AI-first in everything, from how we build and ship to how we think about problems

Enterprises want agents that can do real work on their own data. That data sits across documents, databases and business systems that were never built for agents to read, and today's agents forget most of what they learn once a session ends.
 Our team builds Sarvam's context engine to solve both problems. The knowledge side brings an enterprise's data together so agents can search it, navigate it and cite where an answer came from. The memory side lets agents remember what they learn over time, about individual users, about teams, and across the organisation. We want both to keep improving as they are used.
 Knowledge and memory for agents is a rapidly evolving field. We want to build at the frontier of it, and to show with measurable results that our approach does better than traditional ones.
 About Sarvam 
 Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.
 What this role promises you 
 You will join a small team and own large parts of the platform. The work is driven by real customer deployments, so what you build gets used quickly and you see what works and what does not. You will also work closely with the teams building Sarvam's models, document AI and inference, which makes it much easier to solve problems that cut across the stack.
 What you'll do 
 Build and run the ingestion pipeline that parses, extracts and indexes large volumes of documents, and keep it reliable when files are messy and external services fail.
 Connect to databases and enterprise systems so agents can work with structured records as well as documents.
 Design how enterprise data is modelled, including the ontology, matching the same entity across sources, and tracing every value back to where it came from.
 Build the retrieval tools agents call, with search, filters and citations, and make them fast and cheap enough for agents to use heavily.
 Build memory for agents at the level of a user, a team and the whole organisation: how it is written, stored, retrieved and kept accurate over time.
 Run evals, find where answers go wrong, and keep iterating until quality improves.
 Work with product and forward-deployed engineers to turn what one customer needs into something the platform does for every customer.
 Write design docs and keep decisions documented.
 Our production stack is Go, with Temporal, OpenSearch and Postgres.
 Who you are 
 We are hiring at 3 to 5 years of experience.
 You have built and run backend or data systems in production, and you have fixed them when they broke.
 You are strong in at least one backend language. Our core is in Go, so Go experience is a plus, and you should be happy to work in it every day.
 You have good fundamentals in data modelling and PostgreSQL.
 You have worked on long-running pipelines and know how to make them safe to retry and recover.
 You have worked on search or retrieval and know how to debug why the right result did not come back.
 You use AI coding tools every day and have a good sense of where they help and where they don't.
 You care about measuring quality, and you are comfortable building the evals to do it.
 Bonus points 
 Experience with knowledge graphs, ontologies, entity resolution or structured extraction.
 Experience building memory for agents or LLM applications.
 Document processing, such as OCR, layout or table extraction.
 Connectors or change data capture for ERP, CRM or other enterprise systems.
 Building on MCP, or serving LLMs and embedding models in production.
 On-prem or air-gapped deployments.
 Experience at an early- or growth-stage startup.

https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/span/98107b13-2.text:
Our Mission 
 SPAN develops products that accelerate the rapid adoption of renewable energy in the home. The flagship SPAN Smart Panel is the first true evolution for the traditional home electric panel, harnessing enhanced technology for metering, monitoring, and control. An expanded product suite of intelligent, integrated solutions radically lowers the cost and complexity of energy upgrades–including solar, batteries and EVs–empowering homeowners to be active, resilient and informed players in the energy market.
 The Team and Role 
 SPAN's Device Software team is responsible for all of the software that is physically embodied in our hardware products. The Gen3 SPAN Panel is a distributed system of STM32H5 (Arm Cortex-M33) microcontroller modules that talk over CAN, meter power in real time, and open or close relays that sit directly between the grid, the home and its solar, battery and EV equipment. When that firmware makes a decision, real current moves.
 We are building a dedicated Functional Safety (FuSa) firmware capability to take Gen3 firmware through certification as a Power Control System under UL 3141 and as Class B control software under UL/IEC 60730-1 Annex H . This is not a checkbox exercise: FuSa at SPAN spans how we architect and partition the firmware, how we detect faults and drive the system into defined safe states, how we test and prove coverage, and how we document and trace every safety requirement back to code. You will work alongside the Gen3 firmware team, systems/compliance engineers and our certification lab to make the panel provably safe.
 What You'll Work On 
 Safety architecture & partitioning — isolating safety-critical code on ARMv8-M TrustZone (Secure / Non-Secure) and MPU privilege levels; defining safety, interface and application thread classes; building the data/work-transfer layer across the safety boundary; packaging safety code as controlled, versioned static libraries.
 FuSa RTOS & toolchain migration — moving every module from FreeRTOS/GCC to a certified RTOS (Keil RTX5 FuSa RTS, CMSIS-RTOS2) and the ARM Compiler 6 for FuSa, including thread safety classes, priorities and clang/newlib porting issues.
 Diagnostics & self-tests — integrating the ST Self-Test Library (CPU register, clock, incremental Flash CRC and March-C RAM tests), internal/external and software watchdogs, program-flow and interrupt monitoring, and root-causing the hard faults that currently gate safe-state responses.
 PCS safety functions — feeder and busbar protection, grid-outage detection and PLL/grid transitions, power and voltage rationality checks, relay feedback verification, and fault state machines that transition the panel into defined safe states (SS1–SS4) within required reaction times.
 Safe inter-module communication — CAN heartbeat supervision and safety-message redesign with CRCs, receiver addressing and sequence numbers.
 Verification & evidence — unit tests with enforced coverage in CI, HITL tests for nominal and abnormal PCS behaviour, fault-injection, static analysis, and the system tests used for certification witness testing.
 Process & documentation — software FMEA, Jama requirement-to-code traceability, coding standards audits, and the Annex H deliverables (development plan, safety requirements, architecture, module design, test reports) submitted for certification.
 Role A — Senior / Staff Firmware Engineer, Functional Safety 
 You will be the technical owner of Gen3's firmware safety case. You'll turn standards clauses and FMEA outcomes into concrete architecture and code, make the hard trade-off calls (what goes in the safety partition, what the safe response to a failed self-test is, what "periodic" means to an assessor), and defend those decisions in front of the certification lab. You'll lead by doing — writing the most critical safety code yourself — while setting the patterns, reviews and standards that the rest of the team follows, and mentoring the Junior FuSa engineer.
 At Staff level , you'll also own the FuSa technical strategy across product lines — setting the safety architecture and process that future hardware inherits, being the final technical voice on safety trade-offs, and growing the team's safety expertise beyond yourself.
 Representative Projects 
 Finalising the partitioning design across every module in the panel (Secure/Non-Secure, privileged/unprivileged, safety classes) and driving it to a working, HITL-tested implementation without destabilising a shipping product.
 Owning the software FMEA for each module with systems engineering — declaring detection times and fault responses for every failure mode and producing the verification evidence behind them.
 Designing the safety-related CAN message protocol (CRC, sequence number, timeout supervision) and the reaction logic on each module.
 Acting as the firmware point of contact for the certification lab (e.g. Intertek / UL) through document review and witness testing.
 Required Qualifications 
 Senior: 6+ years writing production firmware in C and C++ for microcontrollers, with at least 2–3 years on safety-related products. Staff: 10+ years, including technical leadership of a safety-certified product from architecture through certification
 Hands-on delivery of firmware through a functional safety standard such as IEC/UL 60730 (Class B/C), IEC 61508, ISO 26262, IEC 62304, DO-178C or UL 1998 — including producing the safety evidence, not just following the process
 Deep experience with ARM Cortex-M: MPU configuration, fault handlers and hard-fault analysis, and ideally ARMv8-M TrustZone
 Strong RTOS fundamentals — priorities, priority inversion, ISR/thread interaction, stack sizing, deterministic timing
 Practical experience implementing MCU diagnostics: CPU/RAM/Flash self-tests, watchdog strategies, program-flow monitoring
 Experience with safety analyses (FMEA/FMEDA, FTA) and requirements traceability tools (e.g. Jama, DOORS, Polarion)
 Solid test discipline: unit testing with mocks (GoogleTest or similar), coverage targets, HIL/HITL testing, static analysis and coding standards such as MISRA C/C++
 Debugging with JTAG/SWD, logic analysers and oscilloscopes; comfortable with CAN, SPI, I2C, UART
 Able to take an open-ended safety problem, break it down, drive decisions to resolution across firmware, systems, hardware and product, and explain the reasoning clearly to non-specialists and assessors
 Bonus Qualifications 
 STM32 (especially STM32H5/U5/L5) and the ST X-CUBE-STL self-test library
 Keil RTX5 / FuSa RTS, ARM Compiler 6 for FuSa, SafeRTOS, or similar certified toolchains
 UL 3141, UL 1741 / IEEE 1547, or other grid/inverter/power-control standards
 MCUboot or secure boot / OTA in safety-relevant systems
 Experience leading witness testing or audits with a certification body (UL, Intertek, TÜV, CSA)
 Energy metering ICs, relay/contactor control, or power electronics
 Role B — Firmware Engineer (Junior), Functional Safety 
 You will build and prove the safety mechanisms that keep the panel safe. Working closely with the Senior FuSa engineer and the Gen3 firmware team, you'll implement well-scoped pieces of the safety design, write the tests that demonstrate they work, and help produce the evidence that gets us certified. This is a rare chance early in your career to learn functional safety on a real, shipping, grid-connected product — you'll come out of it knowing how safety-critical firmware is actually designed, verified and certified.
 Representative Projects 
 Wiring the incremental Flash CRC and RAM March-C self-tests into the self-test runner on a module, including the post-build CRC script, linker changes and exclusion of DMA regions.
 Expanding unit-test coverage on safety-partitioned code until it meets the CI coverage gate, and writing mocks/fakes for hardware interfaces.
 Building HITL and fault-injection tests (e.g. loss of heartbeat, corrupted CAN CRC, stuck relay feedback) that verify the correct safe-state transition and reaction time.
 Running code audits (coding standard, interrupt/callback, assert/result usage) and bringing code and Doxygen documentation into compliance.

 About the Role

 What You'll Do
 Build test infrastructure: Architect and implement test frameworks and infrastructure, and make architectural decisions about test design patterns and abstractions.

 What You'll Need
 Test automation & frameworks: Extensive Playwright experience (including deep knowledge of fixtures architecture), object-oriented test framework design with layered patterns (PCOM/POM) and scalable abstractions over linear scripts, and API testing/orchestration (REST/GraphQL integrated with UI workflows).
 TypeScript & software design: Advanced TypeScript (generics, decorators, advanced typing patterns, type inference), deep understanding of asynchronous programming, concurrency, and race-condition prevention, and strong software design principles including domain-driven design and patterns (Factory, Builder, Facade, Composite).

 Version control: Expert-level Git, GitHub, and distributed version control workflows.
 Reporting & tooling: Advanced reporting (Allure, Playwright HTML reports, custom solutions), test infrastructure and framework architecture, performance optimization at scale, and npm ecosystem/package management.
 Compensation and Benefits
 Compensation: Top of market salary + bonuses and equity

 Growth: Professional development support, remote workspace setup bonus.

 Location

 Jaipur
 The perfect place for Certers to collaborate, co-work and have face to face meetings.
 Why Certa
 Category leadership. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools - recognition that we're defining the category, not following it.
 Industry recognition. We've been honored across the analyst and awards landscape, including Top Tech and Customer Value distinctions in The Hackett Group's 2026 Risk Management SolutionMap, the ProcureTech100 (Advanced AI and Risk Management categories), and Best Overall eProcurement Software in the FinTech Breakthrough Awards.
 A top place to work. Certa was named one of Forbes' Best Startup Employers in the US. We're a fast-growing company where you'll wear many hats, ship quickly, and shape decisions that matter.
 Real scale with strong backing. We've processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries. We're well-funded by leading investors including Fin Capital, Vertex Ventures, and Point72 Ventures, on the back of an oversubscribed Series B, headed towards Series C.

About Onit 
 We're redefining the future of legal operations through the power of AI. Our cutting-edge platform streamlines enterprise legal management, matter management, spend management and contract lifecycle processes, transforming manual workflows into intelligent, automated solutions. 
 We’re a team of innovators using AI at the core to help legal departments become faster, smarter, and more strategic. As we continue to grow and expand the capabilities of our new AI-centric platform, we’re looking for bold thinkers and builders who are excited to shape the next chapter of legal tech. 
 If you're energized by meaningful work, love solving complex problems, and want to help modernize how legal teams operate, we’d love to meet you. 
 The Software Developer in Test (SDET) designs, builds, and maintains the automation frameworks that safeguard the quality of Onit's AI-driven legal operations platform, spanning enterprise legal management, matter management, spend management, and contract lifecycle management. Working within Pune R&D Engineering, this role develops UI, API, and integration test automation using Playwright and JavaScript, integrates it into Jenkins CI/CD pipelines, and drives automation best practices, test data strategy, and quality metrics across the team. Partnering closely with developers and product teams, the Senior SDET investigates complex failures, performs root cause analysis, and helps the team ship high-quality releases with confidence. 
\n 
 Key Responsibilities 
 • Automation Frameworks: Design, develop, and maintain automation frameworks for UI, API, and integration testing. 
 • Test Development: Write maintainable automated tests using Playwright and API automation, with appropriate coverage of critical workflows, edge cases, and role-based permissions. 
 • CI/CD Integration: Integrate automation frameworks with Allure reporting, Jenkins, and CI/CD pipelines so tests run reliably on every build. 
 • Failure Analysis & Debugging: Analyse and triage automation runs, debug complex issues, perform root cause analysis, and drive fixes with development teams. 
 • Quality Practices: Drive automation best practices, test data strategy, and quality metrics, and report on quality trends to engineering leadership. 
 • Code Quality & Collaboration: Review and merge automation code changes in line with best practices, and partner with developers and product managers to build quality in from the start. 
 Required Skills 
 • 3+ years of experience as an SDET or Automation Engineer in product-based, fast-paced environments. 
 • Strong programming skills in JavaScript (TypeScript a plus). 
 • Hands-on experience building and maintaining test automation with the Playwright framework, including UI and API automation. 
 • Working experience integrating automation frameworks with Allure reports, Jenkins, and CI/CD pipelines. 
 • Experience analysing automation runs, triaging failures, implementing fixes, and reporting results. 
 • Experience conducting code reviews and merging code changes while maintaining best practices and Git-based workflows. 
 • Working proficiency with AI tools (e.g., Claude, GitHub Copilot) to accelerate test creation, debugging, and failure analysis, with the judgment to review and validate AI-generated tests and code. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Working experience with Docker, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud platforms such as AWS.
 Exposure to security testing and role-based permission testing.Test LLM outputs for quality, consistency, safety, and hallucinations, and design evals with rubrics, run execution, and result interpretation.
 Build datasets for agents and MCP integrations, including edge and adversarial cases, and understand agentic workflows (planning, tool calling, step chaining).
 Nice to have: Python for building evaluation scripts, automating test pipelines, and analyzing results.
\n Benefits & Perks That Support You: 
 Onit offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support the whole employee at work and beyond: 
 Health Coverage: Employee and immediate family members. 
 Time Away: Flexible paid time off and 10 company paid holidays annually. 
 Family Support: Exceptional paid leave for birth parents, non-birth parents, and caregivers. Onit also offers surrogacy and adoption reimbursement. 
 Income Protection: 100% employer-paid life and disability insurance. 
 Additional Coverage Options: Voluntary benefits including hospital indemnity, critical illness, accident . 
 Tax-Advantaged Accounts: Flexi, NPS . 
 Community Engagement: One paid volunteer day each year to give back to the community. 
 Our Commitment to Applicants 
 We know that not everyone will check every box in a job description. At Onit, we value diversity, inclusion, and authenticity. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification, we encourage you to apply. You may be exactly who we’re looking for.

About HighLevel:
 HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes. To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently. Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.
 Our people With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.
 Our impact Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that. Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts 
 What are we hiring for?
 The systems that run millions of businesses.
Every month, 2.6 billion messages flow through our platform. Our automation engine enrolls 3.1 billion contacts and executes 21.5 billion workflow actions in the same window - with API traffic peaking at 28,000+ requests per second. If these systems lag, businesses lose leads. If they go down, people lose income.
You haven't built at this scale yet. That's fine - almost nobody has.
What we're hiring for is the engineer who reads those numbers and feels pulled toward them. Who wants to know what a queue looks like when it's absorbing a 10x burst, what an index does at 1.5 TB, what "eventually consistent" actually means when a customer is staring at the screen. You'll work on real production paths from week one — with senior engineers around you who've broken and fixed these systems before. You'll build. You'll break things. You'll learn faster here than anywhere else. 
\n 
 Responsibilities: 
 Build and ship features in Node.js / Go services that sit on real production paths — your code handles live traffic, not toy problems
 Own well-scoped services and components end to end: code, tests, rollout, and monitoring 
 Work with SQL and NoSQL data stores — writing queries, adding indexes, and learning why the schema looks the way it does
 Get hands-on with queues, caches, and rate limiters — the building blocks of every system here
 Ship Vue 3 UIs that consume your own APIs — clean components, sane state management, and realtime updates that don't flicker or drift
 Write design docs for your features and defend them in review — clear thinking, honest trade-offs
 Join the on-call rotation with backup from senior engineers — incidents are where the deepest learning happens
 Ask questions relentlessly, absorb feedback from code reviews, and level up fast
 Requirements: 
 2+ years of backend engineering experience with strong fundamentals in Node.js, Go, or a comparable language — and the drive to go deep in ours
 Working knowledge of queues or async processing — you've used Pub/Sub, Kafka, RabbitMQ, or similar, and want to master delivery semantics, ordering, and backpressure
 Genuine interest in distributed systems — you understand the basics (idempotency, retries, consistency trade-offs) and are hungry to learn the rest by building
 Hands-on with Redis or another cache/in-memory store , even at small scale
 Comfortable with SQL or NoSQL databases — you can model data, write efficient queries, and reason about indexes
 Proficient in Vue 3 or a similar modern frontend framework — solid component design and real experience with state management (Pinia, Vuex, or equivalent)
 You write tests as a habit and can put your design thinking into a clear doc
 AI-native builder — you code with agents daily and are pushing to get accurate, production-quality output from them
 Technical Environment: 
 Languages : Node.js (TypeScript), Go
 Frontend : Vue 3, TypeScript, Pinia, Vite, Tailwind
 Storage : MongoDB, Firestore, Redis, ElasticSearch, ClickHouse
 Infra : GCP — GKE, Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks
 CI/CD : GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes
 Why This Role Most engineers spend years at companies where "scale" means a few hundred requests per second — and never find out what they're capable of.
 Here, the systems are the teacher. Every design decision has a visible consequence at billions of events a month. Every incident is a masterclass. You'll sit in architecture reviews with staff engineers debating storage engines and consistency models — and within a year, you'll be contributing to those debates, not just watching them.
 If you optimize your career for learning velocity, there is no faster track than this. 
 On AI 
 We're past the debate. AI is part of how we build - and we expect you to be hungry for it .
 You already code with agents daily. You're learning what they're good at, where they hallucinate, and how to get accurate, tested, slop-free code out of them fast. You treat AI as a multiplier on your learning speed, not a substitute for understanding.
 If you're still copy-pasting from a chat window and hoping, this isn't the seat for you.
 What you're built for 
 You're deeply curious — you don't stop at "it works," you need to know why it works
 You read post-mortems and system-design write-ups for fun , not because someone assigned them
 You've built things beyond your job description — side projects, internal tools, that one system you rewrote because the old one bothered you
 You take feedback like a gift: code review comments make your next PR better, every time
 When something breaks, your first instinct is curiosity, not panic 
 What Success looks like 
 You own a service or component that the team trusts you on completely 
 You're a dependable on-call engineer — you've debugged real incidents and shipped the fixes
 Your design docs have gone from "reviewed heavily" to "approved with nits"
 Senior engineers pull you into harder problems — because you've earned it 
 You're visibly on the path to SDE-3, and everyone around you knows it
 Bonus Points 
 Familiarity with our stack: GCP, MongoDB, Firestore, ClickHouse, ElasticSearch
 You've contributed to a messaging, automation, or event-driven system — at any scale
 Side projects or open-source work that shows you build because you can't not build

 This position is specifically focused on native mobile applications installed and executed directly on Android and iOS devices—not mobile websites, mobile browsers, or responsive web applications. 
 The ideal candidate will have strong proven experience testing native mobile application packages (APK/AAB and IPA), combining JMeter/BlazeMeter protocol-level load testing with BrowserStack real-device native application automation to assess end-user responsiveness, application stability, backend scalability, and overall performance.
 The successful candidate must be capable of independently developing performance test frameworks, implementing realistic native mobile application workloads, executing distributed load tests, automating native application user journeys on real devices, and diagnosing performance bottlenecks across the mobile device, application, network, APIs, and backend infrastructure.

 Key Responsibilities 
 Native Android and iOS Application Performance Testing 
 Design and execute performance tests for native Android and iOS mobile applications , rather than browser-based mobile applications.
 Test installable mobile application packages (APK/AAB and IPA) across real Android and iOS devices.
 Develop realistic workloads representing critical native application business transactions, user journeys, and production usage patterns.
 Measure native application startup and launch times, screen transition times, transaction completion times, responsiveness, and stability.
 Evaluate mobile application CPU utilization, memory consumption, rendering performance, battery impact, and application crashes using appropriate device-level instrumentation.

 Identify performance bottlenecks involving native application code, mobile SDKs, device resources, API communication, and backend infrastructure.
 Evaluate performance differences across device models, hardware configurations, Android/iOS versions, and network conditions.
 JMeter and BlazeMeter Performance Engineering 
 Develop, enhance, and maintain sophisticated JMeter scripts that simulate backend API traffic generated by native Android and iOS applications.
 Implement advanced HTTP(S)/REST scripting, correlation, parameterization, JSON processing, authentication handling, and dynamic test data.
 Configure and execute distributed performance tests using BlazeMeter.
 Design and execute load, stress, spike, endurance, capacity, scalability, and resiliency tests.
 Establish realistic workload models covering concurrent users, transaction distribution, pacing, think time, and ramp-up/ramp-down patterns.
 Analyze response-time percentiles, throughput, transaction rates, error rates, and infrastructure utilization.
 Build reusable performance testing frameworks and integrate automated tests into Agile and CI/CD pipelines.
 Correlate backend load-test results with performance observations from native Android and iOS devices.
 BrowserStack Native Mobile Application Testing

 Use BrowserStack App Automate, App Live, and applicable real-device capabilities for testing installed mobile applications.
 Develop and maintain native mobile automation scripts using Appium or equivalent mobile automation frameworks.

 Investigate performance differences across Android and iOS devices, operating system versions, and network configurations.

 Collaborate with native Android/iOS developers, DevOps, application architecture, and infrastructure teams.
 Assess testing environment readiness, device coverage, monitoring availability, and test-data requirements.
 Participate in Agile sprint activities and incorporate native mobile performance testing into continuous delivery.
 Prepare comprehensive performance reports, bottleneck analyses, and actionable recommendations.

Job Summary
We are seeking a Senior C# Backend Developer to lead the migration of our core business logic from a monolithic SQL Server database into a modern, Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA). API Development: Design, secure, and maintain high-performance RESTful APIs and web services.
Decouple Architecture: Transition the current monolithic setup into a decoupled, service-oriented ecosystem.
Optimize Data Flow: Implement efficient Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) tools like Entity Framework Core.
Testing & Quality: Write comprehensive unit and integration tests to ensure migration safety and zero downtime.
Required Technical Skills
C# / .NET Mastery: 5+ years of deep backend development experience using .NET Core or modern .NET.

Data Access: Expert knowledge of Entity Framework Core or Dapper for efficient data mapping.
Security: Solid understanding of API security protocols, including OAuth2, OpenID Connect, or JWT.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with message brokers (Prefer MSMQ or Azure Service BUS) for asynchronous service communication.
Prior experience executing a successful monolith-to-SOA migration.
Familiarity with containerization tools like Docker.
BE/MCA or equivalent degree/experience.

Mentor and train other team members on design techniques and coding standards
Articulate a long term vision for maintaining and scaling our backend systems and the teams running them.
Work with engineers, designers, product managers and senior leadership to turn our product and technical vision into a tangible roadmap every quarter.
Write high quality, well tested code to meet the needs of your customers. Debugging extremely difficult technical problems, and making systems and products both work better and are easier to deploy, own, operate and diagnose.
Review all feature designs within your product area and across the company for cross-cutting projects. Be an owner of the security, safety, scale, operational integrity, and architectural clarity of these designs.

Required Skills and Experience:

You have at least 3+ years of experience in software engineering
You’ve designed, built, scaled and maintained production services, and know how to compose a service oriented architecture.
You write high quality, well tested code to meet the needs of your customers.
You’re passionate about building an open financial system that brings the world together.
You possess strong technical skills for system design and coding

Job description Join Revun as a Full-Stack Developer to scale web applications using cutting-edge technology. Build robust API integrations and enhance coding with AI tools, working in a fast-paced environment.
 About Revun
 Revun is the software platform and infrastructure layer behind modern property operations. Where other tools solve one piece of the puzzle, Revun unifies leasing, payments, maintenance, communications, compliance, reporting, and brokerage workflows into a single operating system. Owners, property managers, brokerages, leasing teams, maintenance companies, and REITs all operate from the same connected platform, with role-based experiences that adapt to each stakeholder. Based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada.
 About The Role
 As a Full-Stack Developer at Revun, you'll be at the forefront of scaling our web applications. Your day-to-day tasks include reviewing sprint tasks, refactoring backend logic in Laravel, and designing responsive frontends using Tailwind CSS. You will engage with third-party API integration and leverage AI coding assistants to enhance your workflows.
Working closely with the Lead Developer and reporting to the Technical Lead/Founder, your responsibilities include delivering clean, modular code, ensuring zero-downtime deployments, and accelerating development velocity through AI tools. Your success will be assessed by your ability to meet sprint deadlines and ship functional code features consistently.
Within the first 90 days, you'll focus on successfully integrating APIs and leveraging AI tools to accelerate development while maintaining strong code standards. A successful candidate is resourceful, embraces modern coding tools, and communicates progress effectively.
What you will do
 Deliver clean, modular, and scalable code using Laravel and Tailwind CSS or any other modern frontend framework to enhance web application performance and client project outcomes.
 Review sprint tasks, manage pull requests, and refactor backend logic in collaboration with the team, ensuring consistency and quality.
 Write and refactor both backend logic in Laravel and design responsive frontend layouts using Tailwind CSS and Blade components.
 Test and debug third-party API connections, handle complex payloads, and manage error logs effectively.
 Leverage AI coding assistants to draft boilerplate structures, write unit tests, and iterate on feature implementation rapidly.
 Complete assigned feature sprints, conduct code reviews, and test API endpoints to ensure stability and performance.
 Optimize database queries, perform security audits of input validations, and update documentation for integrated modules to maintain system integrity.
 Successfully integrate APIs and leverage AI tools within the first 90 days to accelerate development velocity while maintaining rigorous code standards.
 Troubleshoot unforeseen API documentation errors and resolve merge conflicts or unexpected breaking changes efficiently.
 What we are looking for
 At least 4 years of hands-on experience in web development with SaaS or client applications.
 In-depth experience with PHP and the Laravel framework for building robust applications.
 Strong proficiency in full-stack Laravel development, including backend services and frontend frameworks such as Vue.js or any similar JavaScript framework.
 Hands-on experience integrating REST APIs, payment gateways, and CRM systems like Zoho.
 Solid understanding of MySQL, database schema design, and Git version control workflows.
 Fluent in English, with excellent spoken and written communication skills.
 Clear communication skills in providing progress updates and resolving development issues.
 Nice to have
 Experience in software development within the IT sector.
 Proficiency in AI-assisted development tools like Cursor, Claude, and OpenAI APIs to enhance coding speed and quality.
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
 What we offer
CAD $18,000 to $30,000 per year.
 Benefits
 Remote work flexibility
 Professional development opportunities
 Schedule
Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (EST Timezone).
What happens next
Our recruitment partner will be in touch with you about your application.
If you meet the requirements for the role, they will send you a link to an online video interview that you complete in your own time — there is no appointment to book and nothing to install.
Your completed interview is then shared with us to review alongside your application, and we will let you know what happens next.
Skills Required
Git, Laravel, Payment Gateways, Rest Apis, Php, Crm Systems, Vue.JS, Mysql

Build and evolve our design system. Grow a shared component library (tables, filters, date-range pickers, charts, forms) so teams ship consistent UI faster.

Work with the data layer. Model and query PostgreSQL, and MongoDB, and work with analytical stores for reporting. Spot slow queries and N+1 patterns before they reach users.

Comfort with relational databases (PostgreSQL) and MongoDB, including schema design, indexing, and query optimization.
Experience with the delivery basics: Git workflows, CI/CD, code reviews, and production debugging.

Built or maintained a design system or component library.
Charting experience (Recharts, ECharts, D3, Highcharts) and data-visualization sense.
ClickHouse or BigQuery for analytics and reporting workloads.
Ad-tech, analytics, or B2B SaaS dashboard experience.
Frontend performance work: bundle splitting, Core Web Vitals, rendering large datasets.
Experience building MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers or AI-assisted product features.
Startup experience or meaningful freelance or open-source work.

You think in screens, flows, and the job a publisher is trying to get done, and you push back when a flow doesn’t serve that job.
You write a clean, maintainable React and care about the details users actually notice.
You’re as comfortable opening a Go handler or a slow query as you are a component file, and you’ll build the API when the UI needs something that isn’t there yet.

You enjoy helping other engineers grow and leave codebases better than you found them.

Work on products used by millions, including Pubscale.
Real ownership of the screens and services that publishers and internal teams rely on every day.
A direct line to the CTO and a seat at the table on technical direction.
A learning stipend for books, courses, and conferences (we love curious minds), plus internal blogs.

General Medicine has raised $120M in Series B funding to build the healthcare store.

The round was led by Vineeta Agarwala, MD, PhD, of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and is the largest investment to date from a16z's bio + health team. Read the announcement.

Healthcare needs a store. People should be able to see prices, understand their options, and get advice from clinicians as easily as they shop for anything else. That's what we're building, and this Series B will help us expand the store and reach more customers across the United States.

To learn more, read CEO TJ Parker's post on LinkedIn and the a16z team's post on Substack.

If this sounds interesting, we're hiring. Help us build the store.

About General Medicine

General Medicine is building a healthcare store that makes it radically simpler — and more transparent — for people to access care. We provide upfront cash and insurance prices for visits, prescriptions, labs, imaging, and more.

Behind that simplicity is complex infrastructure: payer integrations, pricing logic, eligibility systems, reconciliation workflows, and financial rails.

We’re building the systems that make transparent healthcare possible.

What we're looking for

We're looking for a frontend engineer to help us build a seamless and beautiful consumer healthcare product on the web. You'll own major surfaces of our Next.js application — from search and scheduling to provider profiles and checkout — and obsess over every detail of the patient experience.

Our ideal candidate has deep expertise in React and TypeScript, a strong eye for UI polish, and experience building fast, accessible, production-grade web apps. You should be comfortable working closely with design to nail interactions and micro-details, but also confident making pragmatic frontend architecture decisions — component patterns, state management, data fetching strategies, performance optimization, and testing. You should also be willing to work across the stack when needed; our frontend talks to a Rails backend, and we value engineers who can trace a bug or build a feature end-to-end.

Beyond frontend expertise, we're looking for someone who cares deeply about technical excellence but is also comfortable moving quickly. We are constantly navigating tradeoffs between engineering velocity and quality. Our ideal candidate is hungry, high-agency, and aspires to be a generalist. Our engineers frequently write product requirements documents, write SQL to understand how features are performing, and own QA — no task is beneath us or outside of the scope of the role if it helps us to deliver a great product. We're looking for someone who can operate in an environment of significant ambiguity, and who is comfortable working closely with design, operations, and clinical stakeholders.

We don't expect you to have a healthcare background (though it's great if you do!). However, you should be excited by the prospect of digging into the messy complexities of the American healthcare system (integrating with EHRs, revenue cycle management, etc).

Qualifications

4+ years of experience building production web applications with React
Strong proficiency in TypeScript and modern React patterns (server components, hooks, data fetching)
Experience with Next.js or a similar framework (routing, SSR/SSG, API routes, caching)
A strong eye for UI quality — you notice when padding is off by 4px and it bothers you
Experience with frontend performance optimization, accessibility, and cross-browser compatibility
Comfort working with RESTful APIs and understanding backend data models
Familiarity with modern backend frameworks is a plus — we use Ruby on Rails and Postgres

Please note that this role is based in our SF office (Spear St). We are hybrid 3x a week.

Compensation: Base is between 150-225k annually + equity options.

Why join us

We're an experienced team that has built a company in this space before, our product has clear product-market fit, and we've raised money from top investors.

We have an ambitious and distinctive vision for what can be built in consumer healthcare. We believe LLMs and price transparency legislation have opened up several massive opportunities.

If you're an ambitious and entrepreneurial frontend engineer and this resonates, please apply.

Mentor engineers, raise engineering standards, and champion modern development practices, including effective use of AI-assisted development.

Strong hands-on software engineering experience with Java/JVM technologies and modern backend frameworks, designing REST APIs, microservices, and distributed systems.

Experience developing and operating scalable applications on AWS or another major cloud platform, with relational and NoSQL databases such as PostgreSQL and Amazon DynamoDB.
Hands-on experience with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, Git and modern software delivery practices, including automated testing across frontend, API and backend layers.
Experience diagnosing complex production and performance problems across the stack using browser developer tools, profiling, logs, metrics and distributed tracing.
Experience mentoring engineers and influencing technical decisions through design reviews, code reviews, hands-on collaboration and sound engineering judgement.


Preferred Experience

Experience with advanced browser technologies such as WebAssembly (WASM), Web Workers, Service Workers, IndexedDB, WebSockets, Streams or similar Web APIs, particularly for building high-performance or computationally intensive web applications.
Experience with Scala or other functional programming languages and functional programming concepts.
Hands-on experience with Python in addition to Java/JVM and frontend technologies.
Experience with Kafka, Redis, Akka, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, or similar distributed technologies.
Experience building customer-facing product capabilities, reusable UI components or design systems that support consistent, intuitive user experiences.
Experience modernizing customer-facing web applications or large-scale distributed systems and improving engineering practices across teams.
Experience effectively using AI-assisted development tools and helping engineering teams adopt and scale these practices across coding, testing, debugging, documentation and code review.


What Success Looks Like

You can take a complex product capability and drive its technical implementation end-to-end, from the browser through APIs and backend services to production.
Architectural direction is translated into high-quality, scalable, production-ready implementations.
Customer-facing web applications and supporting services become more reliable, performant, observable, testable and maintainable while delivering intuitive, high-quality user experiences.
Complex engineering problems across frontend, backend, and distributed systems are resolved with strong technical judgement and effective collaboration with Architects and other engineers.
Engineers around you become more effective through mentoring, design discussions, code reviews, and hands-on technical guidance.
Engineering standards improve through stronger code quality, automated testing, operational readiness, and disciplined implementation.
Engineers around you make effective use of modern development practices, including AI-assisted development, to improve productivity and quality without compromising engineering discipline.
You become a trusted technical leader in your area, known for strong engineering judgement, full stack technical depth, pragmatic decision-making, and the ability to turn complex problems into high-quality solutions quickly.

Job description Senior Full-Stack Engineer (React/Node/TypeScript) — First Engineering Hire, Australian EdTech 
 Remote — Coimbatore preferred; Tamil Nadu / India considered · Full-time · Works directly with the founder in Australia 
 Meeting our criteria: If you don't think you meet the criteria specified below that is okay. Send through your application. We consider all applicants and we'll be back in touch if we think you might be suitable.
 About the role 
 Merit LMS is a live learning platform used by school children, their tutors and administrators in Australia. We're growing from hundreds of students to thousands, and the platform has to be rock-solid before we do. Making it so is this job. It's a TypeScript product: React + Vite on the front end, Express + Prisma + PostgreSQL on the back end, running on AWS, with Stripe billing and AI-assisted marking. 
 We build with Claude Code , an agentic AI coding tool, and that's how we'll keep building. You're not being hired to out-type an AI. You're being hired to take over the technical running of the platform from the founder: decide how things get built, direct the AI agents that build them, and be the last line of defence before anything reaches a child's screen. 
 You'd be the only engineer. The founder is non-technical and is handing the platform over to you, but stays closely involved in the product and makes the business calls.
 How decisions work here (please read this part) 
 The founder makes all business decisions: pricing, what we sell, what we promise families, and what ships when.
 You own the technical and design approach. On work that's been handed to you, you pick the best way to do it. You don't need permission for every choice.
 Good ideas are welcome and expected, but you run them past the founder before building. Nothing significant gets built off your own bat.
 Your authority grows over about six months. You start with minor features and improvements. As trust builds, more of the day-to-day design and prioritisation calls become yours. The founder never fully checks out of the product.
 If you want total autonomy from day one, or you'd rather be handed fully-specified tickets forever, this isn't the job. It sits in between, and it moves. Initially, you may be handed fully specified tickets, then gradually you will be given autonomy.
 What you'll do, day to day 
 Direct AI coding agents through real work: Get AI to write plans, split it into small phases, run the build, and review AI's work.
 Review AI-generated changes sceptically. Most of your value is catching the change that looks right, passes the checks, and is wrong. This is the core skill of the job, not a side task. You are allowed to use AI for all parts of planning, development and testing, but you need to ensure that the AI is guided correctly and it doesn't go off course and ultimately take ownership of the AI's outputs.
 Prove changes work. Trace the code paths yourself and drive the app in a browser before anything ships.
 Own releases end to end: feature switches, database migrations against live data, backups before risky steps, the gated deploy, and the checks after it.
 Write it all down: handover notes, decision records, and the registers of planned improvements and feature switches. This product's continuity lives in its documents, and you'd be their custodian.
 Work a standard 9:00 am to 5:00 pm IST day, so you overlap with Australian afternoons and can talk to the founder live. Close each day with a short written handover (just a Teams message will do).
 What you own 
 Security and children's privacy. Role boundaries between student, tutor and admin; login and session security; making sure no child sees another child's data and no AI output reaches a child unchecked. Anything touching logins, permissions or children's data gets careful human review here, and that review is yours.
 Getting ready to scale. Taking the platform from hundreds of students to thousands: automated tests, monitoring and alerts, performance under load, and infrastructure that grows without breaking.
 Reliability. If the site is down or a child can't finish a lesson, it's yours.
 The release pipeline: GitHub Actions, AWS, process management and environment config.
 Billing correctness. Stripe subscriptions, trials and cancellations. Mistakes here cost families money.
 Code quality over time. Left unchecked, AI agents duplicate code and hide errors. Pushing back on that is the job. Sometimes this can be as simple as managing the context memory of each session, i.e., not letting coding sessions run too long and stopping within, say, 60% to 70% of the context memory used, so the AI doesn't start hallucinating and then get solid handovers to continue in a new session.
 About you (ideally, but all applicants considered) 
 5+ years building and shipping production web applications , strong in TypeScript, React and Node .
 Real experience running database migrations on a live production database with real customer data.
 You've owned a production system alone or nearly alone , and have the instincts that come with it.
 Fluent, sceptical use of AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex or similar). Show us something you directed an agent to build, and tell us about a time you caught it producing something subtly broken.
 Excellent code review. You can read an unfamiliar 500-line change and find the one line that's wrong. Or be good at using AI to do this.
 Clear, plain-English communication with a non-technical person. You explain risk honestly, including when the honest answer is 'I'm not sure'.
 Disciplined written handover. You leave a trail someone else could pick up.
 Reliable daily overlap with Australian hours , and a stable home working setup. A standard 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. workday in Indian time IST fits well with us, as tutoring runs till 8 p.m. in our local time (Australian Eastern time).
 Nice to have 
 Cybersecurity experience, which would be a real advantage. For example: application security and secure code review, penetration testing, hardening logins and sessions, AWS security, threat modelling, or handling a security incident. Certifications (such as OSCP, CompTIA Security+ or AWS Certified Security – Specialty) are welcome but not required.
 Scaling a web app through rapid growth: performance tuning, load testing, PostgreSQL under pressure.
 Adding automated tests to an existing codebase (for example Playwright or Vitest).
 Prisma, PostgreSQL, Express, Tailwind/shadcn, Vite · AWS operations · GitHub Actions · Stripe subscription billing.
 Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and designing for children.
 Previous experience working with sensitive personal data that the law protects (such as children's, health or financial records).
 AI in production: prompt design, provider fallback, cost control.
 What this job is not 
 We'd rather you rule yourself out now than three months in.
 There is no team. No one reviews your work but you and the agents you point at it.
 Automated testing is still being built. Building that safety net is part of your job.
 It's hardening, not greenfield. You'll be making a working, live product stronger and working down a list of known improvements. You won't be starting fresh.
 The codebase carries a lot of process: safety rules, phased work, registers and handovers. It exists because the product serves children and one bad release has real consequences. You need to find that sensible rather than annoying.
 First six months 
 Month 1: learn it. Learn the system, the safety rules and the release process. Ship something small and low-risk, end to end. Start fixing bugs & issues. Getting started on product improvements.
 Months 2–3: build the safety net. Automated tests on the paths that matter most (logging in, lessons, billing), better monitoring and alerts, and a security review of logins, permissions and children's data.
 Months 3–4: take the lead. Work through the list of planned improvements, and lead a feature from plan to release.
 Months 4–6: get ready for scaling. Find and fix what would break with ten times the students (performance, database load, infrastructure), and take on more of the design and prioritisation calls, with the founder's sign-off.
 How we'll assess you 
 Three steps, no more.
 A structured interview about a production system you owned, an incident you handled, and how you use AI coding tools critically.
 A short, paid code-review exercise. We give you an AI-generated change like the ones you'd review here. You tell us what you'd approve, what you'd send back, and what you'd check before it went near a child. This is the actual job. 
 A conversation with the founder about risk, communication, and how you'd say no.
 The package 
 Salary: 10–14 lakh per year, depending on experience.
 Bonus: a performance-based bonus may be paid, at management's discretion.
 Employment: full-time employee in India, employed through an Employer of Record (a company that handles Indian payroll and employment on our behalf).
 Leave and benefits: standard Indian employment terms, provided through the Employer of Record.
 Equipment: we provide a work laptop.
 Tools: we provide your AI coding tools, including Claude Code.
 Location: remote. Coimbatore preferred; Tamil Nadu and the rest of India considered.
 Hours: a standard 9:00 am to 5:00 pm IST working day, for live overlap with Australian afternoons.
 Start: we understand notice periods and will wait for the right person. If you're available for an immediate start, that's a great plus.
 Conditions: offers are subject to background verification and a declaration that you won't hold a second job alongside this one.
 No fees: we will never ask you to pay anything at any stage of hiring.
 How to apply 
 Send your CV (required). A cover letter is optional, but please answer these three questions — a few sentences each is plenty:
 A production system you owned.
 One thing an AI coding agent got wrong that you caught.
 How you'd approach a database migration you can't undo.
 If you have security experience, tell us about that too.
Skills Required
Typescript, React, Express, Cursor, Node, Aws, Postgresql, Stripe

Job description Job Description
 Junior Native Mobile Performance Testing Engineer
 Primary Technologies: Apache JMeter | BlazeMeter | BrowserStack
 Experience Required: 2–4 Years
 Primary Specialization: Native Android and iOS Application Performance Testing
 Position Summary
 We are seeking a motivated, hands-on Junior Native Mobile Performance Testing Engineer with experience in Apache JMeter, BlazeMeter, and BrowserStack to support performance testing of enterprise-native Android and iOS applications.
 This position focuses specifically on native mobile applications installed and executed on Android and iOS devices—not mobile websites, mobile browsers, or responsive web applications.
 The ideal candidate will have practical experience developing and executing performance test scripts, working with REST APIs, supporting cloud-based load tests, and automating native mobile application scenarios on real devices.
The engineer will work alongside senior performance engineers, mobile developers, and infrastructure teams to execute performance tests, collect and analyze results, identify performance issues, and contribute to improving native mobile application responsiveness, stability, and scalability.
This is a hands-on technical position requiring foundational performance testing knowledge, strong scripting and troubleshooting capabilities, and a willingness to develop advanced mobile performance engineering skills.
 Key Responsibilities
 Native Android and iOS Application Performance Testing
 Assist in developing and executing performance tests for native Android and iOS applications.
 Perform performance validation of installed native mobile applications using Android APK and iOS IPA packages.
 Execute test scenarios covering application launch, screen navigation, user interactions, and critical business transactions.
 Measure and document application response times, transaction completion times, and overall responsiveness.
 Support testing across different Android and iOS devices, operating system versions, and network conditions.
 Collect application logs, execution results, and available device performance metrics.
 Assist in identifying performance issues related to mobile applications, network connectivity, APIs, and backend services.
 Execute test scenarios and analyze results under normal and elevated backend load conditions.
 JMeter and BlazeMeter Performance Testing
 Develop, maintain, and execute JMeter scripts for REST API and HTTP(S) performance testing.
 Implement basic to intermediate parameterization, correlation, assertions, JSON extraction, and test-data management.
 Configure and execute load tests using BlazeMeter under guidance from senior engineers.
 Support load, stress, spike, and endurance testing activities.
 Execute predefined workload models involving concurrent users, transaction pacing, and ramp-up/ramp-down configurations.
 Monitor and analyze response times, throughput, transactions per second, error rates, and response-time percentiles.
 Troubleshoot script execution errors, authentication failures, and test-data issues.
 Maintain reusable performance testing scripts and documentation.
 BrowserStack Native Mobile Application Testing
 Execute native Android and iOS application tests using BrowserStack real-device infrastructure.
 Develop, maintain, and execute mobile automation scripts using Appium or equivalent automation frameworks.
 Automate native application interactions, including login, screen navigation, user actions, and business workflows.
 Configure and execute test scenarios across different physical Android and iOS devices.
 Support parallel execution of BrowserStack native application automation and JMeter/BlazeMeter backend load tests.
 Capture native application execution timings, logs, and available device diagnostics.
 Assist senior engineers in correlating real-device application responsiveness with backend API performance.
 Important: Candidates must have experience with or demonstrate practical knowledge of native mobile application testing. Experience limited to testing websites through mobile browsers is not sufficient.
 Performance Monitoring, Analysis, and Reporting
 Monitor application and infrastructure performance using tools such as Dynatrace, Datadog, AppDynamics, Splunk, or comparable platforms.
 Collect and analyze performance test execution results, logs, and monitoring data.
 Identify performance trends, elevated response times, transaction failures, and resource utilization issues.
 Assist senior engineers with performance bottleneck investigation and root cause analysis.
 Document performance defects with supporting evidence and reproducible test conditions.
 Prepare test execution summaries, performance metrics, charts, and status reports.
 Work with development, DevOps, and infrastructure teams to validate fixes and execute performance regression tests.
 Participate in Agile sprint activities and support in-sprint performance testing.
 Required Technical Skills
 Apache JMeter: Hands-on experience creating and executing HTTP(S)/REST API performance test scripts.
 BlazeMeter: Working knowledge of cloud-based load execution, performance test configuration, monitoring, and reporting.
 BrowserStack: Practical experience with or strong working knowledge of native Android/iOS application testing on real devices.
 Mobile Automation: Working experience with Appium or a similar mobile application automation framework.
 Native Mobile Applications: Understanding of installed Android APK and iOS IPA applications, application navigation, API communication, and mobile application behavior.
 API Testing: Experience with REST APIs, HTTP methods, request/response validation, JSON, and authentication.
 Scripting: Knowledge of Java, JavaScript, Python, or another relevant scripting language.
 Performance Metrics: Understanding response time, throughput, concurrency, transaction rates, error rates, and resource utilization.
 Monitoring: Basic experience with an APM or observability solution.
 Defect Management: Experience documenting, tracking, and retesting performance issues.
 Required Experience And Qualifications
 2–4 years of experience in software performance testing, QA automation, or a related engineering role, with practical exposure to performance testing.
 Hands-on experience developing and executing JMeter performance scripts.
 Working knowledge or project experience with BlazeMeter.
 Exposure to BrowserStack real-device testing of native Android or iOS applications.
 Experience developing or executing Appium-based native mobile automation scripts.
 Basic understanding of native mobile application architecture and backend API interactions.
 Familiarity with performance test execution, metric collection, result analysis, and reporting.
 Experience working in Agile software development environments.
 Strong problem-solving, troubleshooting, and communication skills.
 Ability to work independently on assigned testing activities while collaborating with senior engineers.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience testing both native Android and iOS applications.
 Experience executing mobile automation in parallel with backend load tests.
 Familiarity with Android Studio Profiler, Apple Instruments, or other native mobile diagnostic utilities.
 Knowledge of mobile application CPU, memory, startup-time, rendering, and battery performance metrics.
 Experience with mobile network conditions such as Wi-Fi, 4G, and 5G.
 Familiarity with AWS or other cloud platforms.
 Experience with Git, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, or other CI/CD tools.
 Experience with application monitoring platforms such as Dynatrace or Datadog.
 Knowledge of Android App Bundles (AAB) and mobile application distribution.
 Traditional web application performance testing.
 Exposure to Tricentis NeoLoad or other commercial performance testing tools.
 Web performance testing is a secondary, nice-to-have skill and does not replace native mobile application testing experience.
 Expected Outcomes
 The Successful Candidate Will Be Expected To
 Develop and maintain reliable JMeter performance test scripts.
 Successfully execute BlazeMeter load tests and document the results.
 Execute automated native Android/iOS application scenarios on BrowserStack.
 Support concurrent backend load testing and real-device mobile performance validation.
 Collect relevant performance metrics, logs, and application diagnostics.
 Identify and document performance issues for investigation by senior engineers and development teams.
 Produce accurate test execution reports and performance summaries.
 Contribute to reusable performance testing assets and continuous testing improvements.
 Demonstrate increasing independence in native mobile performance testing activities.
 Technical Screening Questions
 Native Mobile Application Testing
 What is the difference between testing a native Android/iOS application and testing a website in a mobile browser Describe your experience testing installed APK or IPA applications.
 JMeter Performance Scripting
 Explain how you would create a JMeter script to test a REST API used by a native mobile application. How would you handle authentication, parameterization, and dynamic response values
 BlazeMeter Test Execution
 Describe your experience executing performance tests using BlazeMeter. How do you configure a test, monitor its execution, and interpret response times, throughput, and error rates
 BrowserStack and Appium
 How would you use BrowserStack and Appium to execute a native Android or iOS application test What types of application interactions and execution metrics would you capture
 Performance Testing and Analysis
 If a native mobile application becomes slow while a JMeter load test is running against its backend APIs, what information would you collect to help determine the cause of the performance degradation
 Senior vs. Junior — Responsibility comparison
 This matrix can help recruiters distinguish between the two positions.
