About MyAdvice
MyAdvice is an established, profitable company with a long history in the markets we serve. We have made a fast, deep shift toward AI-enabled solutions and operate with the urgency and standards of a startup. We are fast-moving and aggressive. We need results-oriented people on our team who will never be satisfied with the status quo and will work hard toward continuous improvement.

What we do. MyAdvice provides an AI-powered system that reduces manual work and cost while helping clients grow revenue. The Success Center, powered by Mya, unifies growth activity across channels and automates workflow execution.

Our mission. We make it easy to profitably grow your business.

How we work. GREAT means Gritty, Resourceful, Expert, Accountable, and Tenacious. We expect hard work, extreme ownership, and extreme accountability. We are willing to do the difficult work required to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients and our colleagues.“We are going to relentlessly chase perfection, knowing full well we will not catch it, because nothing is perfect. But we are going to chase it because, in the process, we will catch excellence.” — Vince Lombardi

The opportunity
We're hiring the front-end owner of a new website platform: the engineer responsible for everything a client, a marketer and a patient actually see and touch.

MyAdvice powers the websites of thousands of medical, dental and legal practices. Today those sites live on a fragmented legacy stack, each one built and patched by hand. We're replacing all of it with one platform built on Next.js and Payload, where a new client site is provisioned in minutes, and we're building a generative AI pipeline that will design, lay out and populate it.

The back end of that platform has owners: multi-tenancy, the data model, provisioning and infrastructure. What it needs now is someone who owns the experience layer as seriously as they do. That means the editor people build pages in, the component library every site is assembled from, the theming system that makes each site look bespoke from one codebase, and the rendering and performance work that decides whether those sites get found.

Two things make this job unusual, and you should know both before you apply.

We are building our own editor, not configuring someone else's. Payload's admin is built for developers, and there is no client-ready page builder we can drop in. We evaluated the off-the-shelf options and decided against them. So the editor is ours to build, over Payload's native blocks schema, working inside the framework's admin internals. This is the deep end of Payload, and it is the hardest and most consequential front-end work on the platform. Thousands of practice staff who use Elementor, Divi or Gutenberg today will land in what you build.

The AI generates configuration, never code. One framework, one component set, unlimited variation through data. The pipeline emits schema-validated JSON: a token set, a section composition, per-block style properties. Your component library and token system are the vocabulary that output is written in, which means the quality ceiling of every generated site is set by what you build.

Every improvement you make ships to every site at once. A 200ms LCP win is not one page, it is the whole fleet.

You'd join a small, Website Platform team: a platform engineer on the application and infrastructure layer, a full-stack builder, a senior architect who knows our existing systems deeply and advises across the project, and our AI engineering group on the generation pipeline. You'd report to our VP of Engineering.

What you'll own

The editor. Our own editing experience, built over Payload's native blocks schema, that non-technical marketers and delivery staff can move fast in without being able to break a site. Drag and drop, live preview, undo, validation, and guardrails that hold. This is product engineering inside a framework's internals, and it is the centre of this role.
The component library. The blocks every site is assembled from: heroes, provider directories, location maps, before-and-after galleries, review carousels, forms. Typed, accessible, tested, documented, and composable enough that the AI pipeline can assemble them as reliably as a person can.
The theming system. One codebase, per-tenant design tokens, genuinely distinct sites, zero per-tenant code. You'll own the token vocabulary and the mechanism that applies it. You'll also hold the line that keeps it working: tokens rather than per-block overrides, no escape hatch for custom CSS, new variants earning their place through review rather than accumulating.
Rendering and performance. The Next.js App Router rendering strategy, covering server components, static generation, caching and revalidation, and Core Web Vitals across the whole fleet. You measure before you claim, and you set the performance budgets that keep new work from regressing.
SEO in the markup. Semantic HTML, metadata, and valid schema.org structured data for practices, providers and locations. These sites exist to be found.
Accessibility. WCAG 2.1 AA as a floor, not an aspiration. Healthcare websites serve patients of every ability, accessibility failures are a legal risk for our clients, and contrast and a11y checks are a gate that generated output has to pass before it ships.
Rendering what the AI generates. The pipeline produces a layout and content as data. Your components and editor turn that into a site a practice will put its name on. You'll work with our AI engineers on the contract between the two, and make sure a generated page can always be opened, understood and fixed by a person.
Handling patient media correctly. Before-and-after imagery is protected health information, and it flows through the upload path and gallery components you build. You'll be responsible for getting consent state, access control and provenance right in the front end, with our architect and compliance work behind you.
The front-end quality bar. Testing strategy covering unit, component, visual regression and end-to-end, front-end CI checks, code review standards, and the patterns the rest of the team follows.

What you'll work within
Two constraints are worth stating plainly, because they shape the work and we would rather you know now.
The page schema is frozen early and deliberately. It is the one commitment on this platform that is expensive to reverse, so it gets locked in the first phase and changes after that are rare and deliberate. You'll be building a large component library inside a schema you cannot casually reshape.
We also expect to work with an external build partner during the build phase, who will contribute code and then exit. Part of this role is reviewing what they produce and owning it afterwards, which is a real responsibility and also a fast way to see the whole surface of the platform.

What we're looking for

We care about what you have shipped and can show us, not what is listed in your skills section. Specifically:
5+ years building production front ends, with React and TypeScript as your daily tools. You've shipped and maintained real applications, not prototypes.
Next.js in production, ideally the App Router. You can explain when you'd render on the server, statically or on the client, and you've lived with the caching consequences.
You've built custom editing or admin UI inside a framework you didn't write. Payload admin components, Sanity Studio customisation, Strapi admin plugins, a custom canvas over a CMS data model, or comparable depth elsewhere. We want evidence you can work inside someone else's framework internals rather than only on top of a clean API. This is the requirement we weigh most heavily.
You've built a component library or design system that other engineers used. You've designed component APIs, versioned them, documented them, and dealt with the requests to bend them.
You've rendered UI from data. Server-driven UI, a block or schema-based renderer, layouts described as JSON rather than written as JSX. You understand what makes a component set composable by a machine rather than only by a person.
Measured performance work. You've moved a Core Web Vital, whether LCP, INP or CLS, and can tell us the before, the after, and what you changed.
Accessibility you can demonstrate. Keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA used correctly, and testing with real assistive technology, not just a passing Lighthouse score.
You test your front end. Component tests with Jest or Vitest and Testing Library, plus end-to-end or visual regression tests with Playwright, Cypress or similar, are part of how you ship.
Enough back end to be dangerous. You're comfortable reading and writing Node.js and working against a headless CMS or API, even if the server isn't your main job.
You raise the bar around you. Code review, patterns, documentation, mentoring.
AI-native. You use Cursor, Claude or similar to build faster, and you own the judgment about what is safe to ship to a live fleet.
Overlap with US colleagues. Comfortable working 2pm to 11pm IST with real-time collaboration.
Things that would make us especially excited
Payload specifically, or depth in another headless CMS such as Strapi, Sanity, Contentful or Directus.
You've built a page builder, a visual canvas, or editing tools used by non-technical people at scale.
Design-token systems or theming engines serving many brands from one codebase.
Schema.org structured data and technical SEO at scale.
Experience with regulated or sensitive media, whether HIPAA, consent management, or access-controlled assets.
Migrating sites off WordPress or another legacy stack.
Integrating LLM-generated content or layouts into a real product.
Open-source front-end contributions we can read.
Missing several of these is fine. Depth in the fundamentals, and evidence you've owned something real, matter more than a full checklist.

How we hire
A short written assessment and a recorded walkthrough of front-end code you're proud of, in your own words.
A conversation with our VP of Engineering about what you've built and how you think.
A technical session with the team: a front-end exercise in TypeScript and React, and a discussion of how you'd approach the editor and theming problems.
We move quickly and tell every candidate where they stand.

Position Overview

We are looking for a Software Engineer, Revenue Cycle Management AI Automation & Platform to help build the next generation of Experity’s RCM technology.

In this role, you will design, develop, deploy, and operate production-grade software that supports critical healthcare revenue cycle workflows. You will work primarily across backend services, APIs, integrations, event-driven and long-running workflows, configurable business rules, and data, supporting areas such as charge entry, claims processing, claim submission, rejection and denial resolution, payments, and other parts of the revenue cycle.

You will work closely with Product Managers, RCM Operations, Software Engineers, Architects, Data teams, and QA to translate complex healthcare business workflows into scalable, maintainable software solutions.

This is a product engineering role where success means more than delivering features. You will help increase automation, reduce unnecessary manual work, improve claim outcomes, shorten processing time, and build an RCM platform that can continue to evolve.

You will be expected to understand the business workflow behind the software you build, identify opportunities for automation, and use deterministic software, configurable rules, data, and AI agent based on what is most appropriate for the problem.

What You’ll Do
Design, develop, test, deploy, and operate scalable production software supporting Experity’s Revenue Cycle Management workflows.
Build backend services and REST APIs using TypeScript, Node.js, and cloud-native technologies.
Contribute to modern web applications when needed using technologies such as React, Next.js, and TypeScript.
Design and implement event-driven, queue-based, and asynchronous workflows with explicit state management, retries, redrive, exception handling, idempotency, and auditability.
Design long-running RCM workflows that support state transitions, human-in-the-loop processing, exception handling, replay/recovery, workflow versioning, and compensation or reversal when appropriate.
Build integrations with Experity applications, healthcare clearinghouses, payer systems, and third-party RCM services.
Design reliable interfaces for claims, payment, eligibility, rejection, denial, and other healthcare transaction workflows.
Develop configurable business rules and workflow capabilities that replace logic currently distributed across application code, spreadsheets, and operational processes.
Build rules and workflow capabilities that are configurable, versioned, explainable, auditable, and safe to change without introducing unnecessary application dependencies.
Work with claims, financial, and operational data to improve automation, identify exceptions, and measure business outcomes.
Integrate Generative AI, LLMs, agents, retrieval, and machine learning capabilities where they provide measurable value, while using deterministic software and business rules where those approaches are more appropriate.
Build AI-enabled capabilities using clearly defined tools, APIs, contracts, permissions, validation, evaluation, observability, and fallback paths rather than treating LLMs as standalone solutions.
Use modern AI-assisted software development practices for codebase exploration, development, testing, debugging, documentation, and engineering productivity while maintaining appropriate engineering review and quality standards.
Build observability, automated testing, security, operational controls, and failure recovery into software from the beginning.
Design systems with healthcare security, PHI protection, least-privilege access, auditability, and safe operational logging in mind.
Contribute to architecture, technical design, engineering standards, and platform evolution.
Collaborate with Product, RCM Operations, Architecture, Data, QA, and other engineering teams to understand real-world workflows and translate them into reliable software.
Investigate production issues using application behavior, logs, metrics, data, and user workflows.
Own software through production and continuously improve it based on system behavior, operational feedback, and business results.
Measure the impact of engineering improvements through outcomes such as automation rate, exception rate, manual touches, processing time, rejection/denial resolution time, successful resubmission, payment outcomes, and system reliability.

Required
3+ years of professional software engineering experience building and supporting production applications.
Strong software engineering fundamentals, including application design, testing, debugging, code review, and maintainability.
Experience building backend services, REST APIs, and distributed applications.
Proficiency with TypeScript, Node.js, or comparable modern backend technologies.
Experience with modern web development technologies such as React, Next.js, or similar frameworks.
Experience with relational databases, SQL, data modeling, and transactional systems.
Experience developing and operating cloud-hosted applications, preferably on AWS.
Understanding of asynchronous processing, queues, events, retries, idempotency, and distributed-system failure modes.
Experience with automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, observability, and secure software development practices.
Ability to break complex business workflows into well-defined software components, services, and contracts.
Ability to investigate ambiguous problems and develop solutions using production behavior, data, logs, and user workflows rather than relying only on predefined requirements.
Strong collaboration and communication skills with the ability to work across engineering, product, operations, architecture, and data teams.
Preferred

Experience in one or more of the following areas is valuable but not required:

Healthcare Revenue Cycle Management, medical billing, claims, rejections, denials, eligibility, or payment processing.
Healthcare, HealthTech, or SaaS environments.
Waystar or other healthcare clearinghouse integrations.
High-volume transaction or workflow-processing systems.
Event-driven architectures and distributed systems.
Modernizing legacy systems incrementally while maintaining production continuity.
Configurable rules engines, workflow orchestration systems, or exception-management platforms.
Production use of Generative AI, LLMs, AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation, or machine learning.
AI orchestration frameworks, structured tool use, MCP or similar tool protocols, and agentic workflows.
Build human-in-the-loop automation where AI or software recommendations require review, approval, correction, or escalation.
Snowflake or other cloud-native data platforms.
Docker, Kubernetes, and containerized application deployment.
Data-intensive application development and distributed data processing.

Backend: TypeScript, Node.js, Python
Frontend: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS

We want engineers who understand the problem they are solving, not just the ticket they are implementing.

You should be comfortable learning a complex healthcare domain, questioning existing processes, working through ambiguity, making practical technical tradeoffs, and taking ownership of the software you build.

Our engineers collaborate closely with business and operational teams because understanding the real workflow is essential to building the right solution. We value pragmatic engineering, measurable outcomes, incremental modernization, and choosing the right technology for the problem rather than applying technology for its own sake.

We expect engineers to think beyond individual features: understand the end-to-end RCM workflow, identify where AI and automation can eliminate unnecessary work, design for exceptions and failure from the beginning, and measure whether the software actually improves operational and financial outcomes.

We are also building an AI-native engineering culture. Engineers are expected to use modern AI development tools thoughtfully to accelerate delivery and improve quality while retaining ownership of architecture, code quality, testing, security, and production outcomes.

Our merchants embed Glomo directly into their own apps, which means our mobile SDKs are the product for a large part of our business. Today those SDKs are Flutter and React Native wrappers around our web checkout. That was the right call to get to market. It is no longer enough. Over the next year we're taking mobile in-house and going native: first-class Android and iOS SDKs, and native capability inside the cross-platform ones — camera-based document capture, liveness, secure file handling, on-device identity and biometrics. You'll be the engineer who does that. You'll work alongside a senior mobile engineer, and you'll own delivery from day one.

 real-world devices.
 Secure file handling — pickers, uploads, encryption at rest, temp-file hygiene.

 Support merchants for real
 Debug integration issues inside someone else's app, with partial information, on a device you

hungry for an opportunity to prove themselves on a real product, not just maintain old code

reliable automation of multi-step web workflows, with proper handling of sessions, timeouts, errors and retries
always secure, and respecting each website’s rules

Help guide interns and freshers on daily tasks and code.

Must-have skills

2–3 years of hands-on software development experience.
Strong Python with FastAPI. Experience with Flask or Django also counts.
React (with JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, CSS).
PostgreSQL: good SQL, table design, joins, indexes.
REST API design: authentication (JWT/sessions), validation, error handling.
Browser automation: hands-on experience with Selenium or Playwright.
Git, and writing clean, readable code.
AI-first working: daily use of AI coding tools, with real examples of how it helped you deliver faster.
Good communication in English. Telugu or Hindi is a plus.

Strong plus

Redis, and background job queues (Celery, RQ, ARQ, RabbitMQ or similar).
WebSockets and async Python (asyncio).

Windows desktop or tray apps, and packaging Python apps (PyInstaller, Nuitka, Inno Setup, MSI).

S3 or other object storage.

Vite, React Query, Tailwind CSS or similar modern frontend tools.
Node.js or another backend language.

Someone looking only for a comfortable, routine job.
Someone who copies AI-generated code without understanding or checking it.
Someone who builds automation that works once and breaks often.
Someone who wants to restart everything from scratch. We build carefully on the work already done.

Give every app and agent a company builds its superpowers: AI, integrations and computers it can use.

The role

The apps and agents people build on Isomorph need to think with the best AI models, work with every tool the company uses, react to what happens in the business, and even operate websites and software that have no API, by using a computer like a person would.

You will build those superpowers, once, for everyone. You will also own the AI software factory that lets a small team build a platform this ambitious. This is the role for someone who wants to work on the most frontier parts of the stack.

What you’ll own
Computer use: agents that get real work done in websites and software no API can reach.
AI for every app: the best models, within each company’s budgets and rules.
Integrations that connect apps and agents to every tool a company runs on.
Apps that work together, turning a company’s software into a network.
The AI software factory we use to build Isomorph itself.
What you’ll get to build next
Learn from real work done across many companies, which over time becomes the foundation for models of our own.
Build agents that do real work across a company’s apps and systems, safely.
Build a platform that runs itself, with agents handling operations, reliability and security for every app.
You’ll thrive here if
You have built platform capabilities that other products depend on.
You have shipped AI models and agents in production and made them dependable.
You have connected to many external systems and know where they break.
You love breadth, and switching between very different hard problems.
Why Isomorph

For fifty years, software inside a company has been written by a small group of engineers, for everyone else. That is ending. With AI, the people who know the work best (the finance analyst, the ops lead, the recruiter, the support manager) can now build the software they need themselves. Most of them have never written a line of code.

This is one of the biggest shifts in how companies work, and it has a missing piece. The software these people build is useful, and very often unsafe: no sign-in, sensitive data exposed, nobody to run it, and invisible to IT. Multiply that across a large company and you get thousands of apps and agents that nobody governs.

Isomorph is the foundation that software runs on. Bring an app or agent built with any AI tool, and Isomorph runs it on the company’s own cloud: secured, connected to company data and systems, monitored and kept healthy. Builders never think about infrastructure. IT stays in control of everything.

We believe every company will become AI-native one workflow at a time, built by its own people. Isomorph is where that software will live.

The team. You will join a small, high-talent-density founding team from IIT Madras and IIT Delhi. The founders are second-time founders who have built companies before and sold one.

Why you’ll love it here
You’ll be early. You will be one of the first people on the team, with real ownership and a real say in what Isomorph becomes.
You’ll work at the frontier. AI agents and enterprise-grade infrastructure, applied to a problem every company is about to have.
You’ll see your impact. We work side by side with customers, so what you ship is in real people’s hands within days.
You’ll build the way the future builds. We build Isomorph with AI agents ourselves, so your leverage is your judgment and your taste, not your typing speed.
You’ll grow fast. Small team, huge surface, founders who have built and scaled before.

Apply: https://isomorph.ai/careers/founding-engineer-platform-capabilities/

About Gen

Gen is a global company dedicated to powering Digital Freedom through its trusted consumer brands including Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion and more. Our combined heritage is rooted in financial empowerment and cyber safety for the first digital generations, and today we deliver award-winning cybersecurity, online privacy, identity protection and financial wellness solutions to nearly 500 million users in more than 150 countries.

Together, we share a collective passion and vision to protect consumers and help them grow, manage and secure their digital and financial lives. We’re always looking for smart, fearless and high-impact talent who see AI as a teammate – leveraging it to move faster and deliver meaningful results.

When you’re part of Gen, you’ll have the flexibility, tools and support to do your best work and grow your career – from flexible working options and time off to competitive pay, benefits and well-being programs.

At Gen, we are scrappy and relentlessly customer driven. We create room for healthy debate, experimentation and continuous learning, and we seek out people with different experiences, identities and ideas to join our team. You’ll work with people who back each other, respect each other and understand that our differences are a competitive advantage.

About the Role

AI is already part of every stage of how we build products, from ideation and design to coding, testing and release. The next step is agentic: AI agents that plan, write, test and ship real mobile code, with engineers designing, directing and reviewing them. We want engineers who build those agents, not just use them.

As an AI-First Mobile Engineer, you will build across the whole mobile stack of Norton, Avast, AVG and Avira apps used by tens of millions of people: the screens and flows users touch every day, and the shared code underneath them. You will work across:

App UI and features: user-facing screens and flows in Jetpack Compose (Android) and SwiftUI/UIKit (iOS), from onboarding and purchase flows to scam protection, VPN, identity and AI-assistant experiences.

Compose Multiplatform (CMP): shared UI across Android and iOS where it makes sense, native UI where it doesn’t.

Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) SDKs: shared Kotlin code for business logic, networking and storage, compiled for Android and iOS.

Native SDKs: the Kotlin (Android) and Swift (iOS) libraries apps use today, and the platform-specific parts of shared SDKs.

You will be strongest on one platform, work across both, and be comfortable anywhere in the stack, from pixel-level UI to SDK internals. This is a principal-level, hands-on individual contributor role. You write production app and library code, and much of it will be written by agents you set up, direct and review. You will design the agentic workflows the rest of the team relies on, and work alongside engineers in Asia, Europe and North America.

Key Responsibilities

Build user-facing features in Jetpack Compose and SwiftUI, from spec to app-store release, including the most complex and highest-risk parts of the apps.

Improve app performance, stability, crash-free rates, startup time, battery use and app size.

Fix critical production issues: crashes, performance regressions and security findings.

Design, build and maintain SDKs used by multiple product teams, in shared Kotlin and in native Android or iOS code.

Own features end to end: API design, implementation, tests, release and support for consuming apps. Keep public APIs stable and migrations short.

Improve how we build, package and release SDKs for both platforms, and measure what our SDKs cost the host app (startup, memory, battery, app size).

Build and run agents that do real engineering work on our apps and SDKs: implementing features from specs, building UI from designs, writing and fixing tests, triaging crashes, upgrading dependencies and moving native code to KMP.

Make our codebases agent-ready: clear architecture docs, agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and similar), fast and reliable tests, and module boundaries an agent can reason about.

Work closely with product, design, backend and QA to achieve the best possible experience for our customers.

Review code from engineers and agents alike, with the judgment to catch what AI gets wrong. Leave the codebase better than you found it.

Write clear specs and design proposals in English that both engineers and agents can build from, and explain trade-offs to engineers, managers and business partners.

About you :

Agents are how you work. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or GitHub Copilot agent mode are your daily tools, and you regularly run several at once on real production work.

You know how agents work under the hood: context engineering, tool design, planning and sub-agents, memory, evals, and where they fail – hallucinated APIs, drift on long tasks, prompt injection.

You have sharp judgment. You know when to trust agent output and when to step in, and you keep AI-written code secure, tested and maintainable.

You can show us. A repo, demo or write-up of an agent or workflow you built, and the measurable difference it made.

8+ t0 15+ years of professional mobile development, with deep expertise in at least one of Android or iOS and at least one app or library shipped at scale.

Strong command of your primary platform’s language, concurrency model and architecture (for example Kotlin and coroutines, or Swift and Swift Concurrency)

Readiness to work on the other platform regularly. Some hands-on experience with it is a strong plus.

Hands-on experience with Kotlin Multiplatform: sharing business logic between Android and iOS, structuring shared modules, handling Swift interop and multiplatform Gradle builds. Production experience is preferred, but substantial side projects you can show us also count.

Modern mobile UI: production experience with Jetpack Compose and/or SwiftUI where needed. You care about UX, accessibility, animation and how the app feels in the hand.

Experience with automated testing (including UI tests), CI/CD, app-store release processes and production monitoring.

Good judgement on API design, compatibility and the cost of breaking changes.

Growth attitude: eager to learn, experiment and push boundaries. You get up to speed on a new product, codebase and business in weeks, not months.

Collaboration: at home in a fast-paced, global team across time zones. You mentor other engineers and work easily with product, design and business partners.

Clear written and spoken English. You can explain a technical trade-off to a non-engineer.

Experience with Compose Multiplatform, ideally in production. If you have built CMP side projects and can show them, we want to talk to you.

Built agents that drive mobile apps end to end: UI automation on emulators and simulators with tools such as Maestro, XCUITest or Espresso, and screenshot-based verification.

Building SDKs or libraries consumed by other teams or third parties.

Job Description Summary
We are looking for a Software Engineer to help build and maintain reusable user interface components for GE HealthCare’s Ethos Design System (EDS).

In this role, you will turn designs into accessible, tested and well-documented components used by product teams across the organization. You will work with senior engineers, UX designers, product owners and quality engineers to deliver consistent user experiences for clinical and operational applications.

You should be comfortable building modern web interfaces and interested in developing deeper skills in Web Components, design systems and accessibility. You will own assigned components and features with guidance from senior team members.

GE Healthcare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description
About EDS

EDS is the unified digital platform that powers GE HealthCare’s global software portfolio. It brings together reusable UI components, design patterns and accessibility standards to connect user experience and engineering.

By encouraging teams to reduce, reuse and recycle, EDS helps product teams eliminate redundant work and build consistent, accessible applications. These foundational components support clinical and operational applications and allow teams to focus on patient safety.

The opportunity

We are looking for a Software Engineer to build and maintain reusable components for the Ethos Design System. As EDS grows across GE HealthCare’s product portfolio, you will help make its components easy for teams to discover, integrate and use.

You will work with senior engineers, architects, UX designers, product owners, Lead System Designers, DevOps and quality engineers. You will own assigned components and features from implementation through testing, documentation and maintenance, with support and guidance from senior team members.

Key responsibilities
Component engineering and API design
Develop and maintain reusable, encapsulated UI components using Lit and Web Components.
Write clean JavaScript and TypeScript, semantic HTML, and scoped CSS using SASS.
Implement component APIs, including properties, events and slots, following established design system patterns.
Investigate defects and contribute to component performance, reliability and maintainability.
Participate in code reviews and apply feedback from other engineers.
Cross-framework integration
Help build, test and maintain component wrappers and integrations for React, Angular and Vue applications.
Investigate integration issues reported by product teams and collaborate with senior engineers on solutions.
Contribute examples and guidance that help teams adopt EDS components.
Design fidelity and accessibility
Work closely with UX designers to understand component appearance, behavior and interaction states.
Use Figma Dev Mode to inspect designs and implement components that match agreed specifications.
Apply WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility requirements, including keyboard navigation, screen reader support, ARIA and color contrast.
Test components for accessibility and address identified issues with support from the team.
Testing, documentation and delivery
Write and maintain unit tests using tools such as Jest or Vitest.
Contribute usage examples and technical integration guidance in Storybook.
Test component behavior across supported browsers and screen sizes.
Participate in Agile ceremonies and maintain assigned work items, estimates and status updates in Rally.
Work with DevOps and quality engineers to support the team’s CI/CD and quality practices.
Ownership and collaboration
Take ownership of assigned components and features through development, testing, delivery and maintenance.

Job Description – Full Stack Developer – MEAN/MERN, Mobile & Agentic AIAbout the Company

TechVibrant Innovative Solutions Pvt Ltd is a Bangalore-based technology company focused on building enterprise software solutions, digital products, mobile applications, and Industry 4.0 solutions for businesses across multiple industries.

We work closely with our customers to understand complex business problems and build scalable, practical technology solutions that improve productivity, customer experience, and business outcomes.

About the Role

We are looking for a Full Stack Developer with 3–4 years of experience who is comfortable working across multiple layers of the technology stack.

You will be responsible for building and enhancing web and mobile applications, developing APIs and backend services, working with databases and integrations, and contributing to end-to-end product development.

This is not a role limited to frontend or backend development. You will have opportunities to work across the frontend, backend, mobile, database, and cloud layers.

Forward-Deployed Engineering & AI Focus
This is a forward-deployed engineering role. You will work closely with customers, business/product stakeholders and internal teams to understand real-world problems, translate them into specifications, build and deploy working solutions, and iterate based on feedback. The role requires strong hands-on engineering skills together with an ability to use AI coding agents and agentic AI capabilities to accelerate the software development lifecycle.

What Will You Work On?

As part of the engineering team, you will:

· Develop and maintain modern web applications using React.js / Angular

· Build scalable backend services and REST APIs using Node.js and Express.js

· Develop and integrate Android and iOS mobile applications

· Design and work with databases such as MongoDB, PostgreSQL and MySQL

· Build integrations with third-party services and external APIs

· Develop new features and enhancements for existing platforms

· Understand existing codebases and independently implement new functionality

· Debug, troubleshoot and optimize applications across different technology layers

· Work with cloud infrastructure, containers and CI/CD pipelines

· Collaborate with product, design and engineering teams to deliver complete features

AI-Native & Agentic Engineering

We are building an AI-native engineering culture, where AI is an integral part of the software development lifecycle.

Our engineering processes increasingly use AI-assisted and agentic workflows for:

· Requirement analysis and clarification

· Specification and Spec-Driven Development (SDD)

· Architecture and technical design

· Code generation and implementation

· Automated testing

· Debugging and issue resolution

· Code reviews and refactoring

· Documentation

· Development workflow automation

You will be expected to learn and work with AI coding agents and AI-assisted development tools as part of your daily engineering workflow.

We are looking for engineers who are curious about how AI can make software development faster, more reliable, and more scalable, while maintaining strong engineering practices.

Required Skills

· 3–4 years of hands-on software development experience

· Strong experience with MEAN/MERN stack development

· Strong experience with Node.js and Express.js

· Experience with modern frontend technologies such as React.js and/or Angular

· Strong experience with MongoDB

· Experience with PostgreSQL and/or MySQL

· Strong understanding of REST API development

· Hands-on experience with Android and iOS mobile application development

· Understanding of authentication, authorization and API integrations

· Good debugging and problem-solving skills

· Ability to work across frontend, backend, database and mobile layers

· Experience working with existing codebases and independently developing new features

Preferred / Desired Skills

· Experience with Spec-Driven Development (SDD)

· Experience using AI coding assistants / AI development tools

· Understanding of AI agents and agentic engineering workflows

· Cloud experience with AWS or Azure

· Experience with Docker

· Experience with CI/CD pipelines

· Experience with microservices architecture

· Experience with automated testing

 Preferred: Prior experience in a forward-deployed engineering, customer-facing engineering, solutions engineering, implementation engineering, or similar role.

 Preferred: Demonstrated ability to use agentic AI capabilities for requirement analysis, technical design, coding, testing, debugging, documentation and workflow automation.

What We Look For

We are looking for engineers who:

· Take ownership of features from requirement to deployment

· Can learn and work across different technology stacks

· Are comfortable understanding and improving existing systems

· Have strong problem-solving and debugging abilities

· Are interested in AI-native software development

· Are willing to adopt new engineering tools, processes and practices

· Can work independently while collaborating effectively with the team

Role Expectation: Candidates should be comfortable working as forward-deployed engineers, engaging directly with stakeholders when required, and applying agentic AI capabilities and Spec-Driven Development in day-to-day engineering work.

The result is unparalleled insights, simplified operations, and higher profitability for your employees and business.  You will build and maintain features across the Essentials web application, its .NET services and its databases, as part of a team split between India and the United States.  Review teammates' pull requests and respond to review on your own. 
 Keep documentation of what you build current, including the instructions and context that coding agents rely on
 Give your manager clear status and risk updates so work stays on schedule. 
 AI-driven development (AIDLC) The team follows an AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC): coding agents take part in every stage of delivery, and engineers direct, check and own the result. This is a core requirement of the role, not a preference.

 Use coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Cursor every day, across requirements, design, implementation, testing, code review and debugging. 
 Turn a user story into a clear, bounded task an agent can carry out: the goal, the constraints, the files and data involved, and how success will be checked. 
 Plan before generating: have the agent propose an approach, challenge it, and agree the design before code is written. 
 Verify everything an agent produces. Read the diff, run the tests, exercise the change in the running application, and reject work you cannot explain. 
 Own what you merge. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand, and you answer for it in review and in production. 
 Keep credentials, customer data and other sensitive information out of prompts and agent context, and follow PDI's AI usage policies. 
 Improve the team's shared setup: project instructions, reusable prompts and skills, test fixtures and other context that make agents more reliable for everyone. 
 Know when not to use an agent and recognize when one is going in circles or producing plausible but wrong output.

 Solid SQL skills on a relational database (SQL Server or PostgreSQL): queries, stored procedures and basic performance tuning. 
 Hands-on experience using coding agents or AI coding assistants in real project work, and the ability to show how you directed and verified their output.

 Habit of writing automated tests for your own code.

That's why we're delivering an integrated portfolio of global, cloud-based solutions and services to meet our customers needs today and well into the future. Our deep domain knowledge is backed by our industry-specific software offerings and a people-first approach. Serving the entire supply chain means that we’ve had to solve a wide range of industry challenges and deliver measurable value. To address the increasingly dynamic convenience retail and petroleum wholesale industry, PDI leads the way with converged digital, cloud-optimized, secure, and scalable solutions including ERP, Loyalty, Fuel Pricing, Point-of-Sale and Logistics to create a broader industry ecosystem. The result is unparalleled insights, simplified operations, and higher profitability for your employees and business. We’re dedicated to helping our more than 1,500 customers in over 50 countries, providing solutions and services to over 200,000 sites.
PDI C-Store Essentials is cloud back-office software for convenience store owners and operators. It covers pricebook and promotions, point-of-sale integration, fuel, lottery, daily paperwork, scan data reporting and subscription billing, for single stores, chains and franchise operators.
You will build and maintain features across the Essentials web application, its .NET services and its databases, as part of a team split between India and the United States. The team works AI-first: coding agents are part of how every engineer plans, builds, tests and reviews work, and this role is expected to use them well from day one.
Job Responsibilities:
Design, build and ship features across the stack: React and TypeScript on the front end, ASP.NET Core services and APIs on the back end, SQL Server and PostgreSQL underneath.
Take part in design decisions for new and existing features, raise risks early and ask for help when blocked.
Work with the Product Owner to clarify requirements, break them into small deliverable pieces and estimate them.
Write automated tests for your own work (xUnit, Vitest, Playwright) and work with QA engineers on test plans and release stabilization.
Troubleshoot and fix development and production issues with urgency, using logs and monitoring to find the root cause.
Review teammates' pull requests and respond to review on your own.
Keep documentation of what you build current, including the instructions and context that coding agents rely on.
Give your manager clear status and risk updates so work stays on schedule.
AI-driven development (AIDLC)
The team follows an AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC): coding agents take part in every stage of delivery, and engineers direct, check and own the result. This is a core requirement of the role, not a preference.
You will be expected to:
Use coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Cursor every day, across requirements, design, implementation, testing, code review and debugging.
Turn a user story into a clear, bounded task an agent can carry out: the goal, the constraints, the files and data involved, and how success will be checked.
Plan before generating: have the agent propose an approach, challenge it, and agree the design before code is written.
Verify everything an agent produces. Read the diff, run the tests, exercise the change in the running application, and reject work you cannot explain.
Own what you merge. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand, and you answer for it in review and in production.
Keep credentials, customer data and other sensitive information out of prompts and agent context, and follow PDI's AI usage policies.
Improve the team's shared setup: project instructions, reusable prompts and skills, test fixtures and other context that make agents more reliable for everyone.
Know when not to use an agent and recognize when one is going in circles or producing plausible but wrong output.
Required Skills & Experience:
Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field plus 4 to 6 years of experience building or maintaining software in a product development environment, or equivalent experience.
Working proficiency in C# and .NET (ASP.NET Core), including building and consuming REST APIs.
Working proficiency in a modern JavaScript framework with TypeScript; React is preferred.
Solid SQL skills on a relational database (SQL Server or PostgreSQL): queries, stored procedures and basic performance tuning.
Hands-on experience using coding agents or AI coding assistants in real project work, and the ability to show how you directed and verified their output.
Computer science fundamentals: object-oriented programming, design patterns, data structures and algorithms.
Practical experience with Git, pull requests, CI/CD pipelines and Agile delivery.
Habit of writing automated tests for your own code.
Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to explain technical concepts in non-technical terms. Clear writing matters more here than usual, because it is also how you direct agents.
Self-starter who can work independently as part of a distributed team, manage competing priorities and learn an unfamiliar codebase quickly.

For nearly 40 years, PDI has helped convenience retailers and petroleum wholesalers adapt to changes in the industry by leveraging the latest technologies. Simplifying the complexity in your world is our main focus. That's why we're delivering an integrated portfolio of global, cloud-based solutions and services to meet our customers needs today and well into the future. From the back office to fuel logistics, and the latest wave of consumer demands and digital commerce, PDI solutions and services are designed to give you a competitive edge. Our deep domain knowledge is backed by our industry-specific software offerings and a people-first approach. Serving the entire supply chain means that we’ve had to solve a wide range of industry challenges and deliver measurable value. To address the increasingly dynamic convenience retail and petroleum wholesale industry, PDI leads the way with converged digital, cloud-optimized, secure, and scalable solutions including ERP, Loyalty, Fuel Pricing, Point-of-Sale and Logistics to create a broader industry ecosystem. The result is unparalleled insights, simplified operations, and higher profitability for your employees and business. We’re dedicated to helping our more than 1,500 customers in over 50 countries, providing solutions and services to over 200,000 sites.
PDI C-Store Essentials is cloud back-office software for convenience store owners and operators. It covers pricebook and promotions, point-of-sale integration, fuel, lottery, daily paperwork, scan data reporting and subscription billing, for single stores, chains and franchise operators.
You will build and maintain features across the Essentials web application, its .NET services and its databases, as part of a team split between India and the United States. The team works AI-first: coding agents are part of how every engineer plans, builds, tests and reviews work, and this role is expected to use them well from day one.
Job Responsibilities:
Design, build and ship features across the stack: React and TypeScript on the front end, ASP.NET Core services and APIs on the back end, SQL Server and PostgreSQL underneath.
Take part in design decisions for new and existing features, raise risks early and ask for help when blocked.
Work with the Product Owner to clarify requirements, break them into small deliverable pieces and estimate them.
Write automated tests for your own work (xUnit, Vitest, Playwright) and work with QA engineers on test plans and release stabilization.
Troubleshoot and fix development and production issues with urgency, using logs and monitoring to find the root cause.
Review teammates' pull requests and respond to review on your own.
Keep documentation of what you build current, including the instructions and context that coding agents rely on.
Give your manager clear status and risk updates so work stays on schedule.
AI-driven development (AIDLC)
The team follows an AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC): coding agents take part in every stage of delivery, and engineers direct, check and own the result. This is a core requirement of the role, not a preference.
You will be expected to:
Use coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Cursor every day, across requirements, design, implementation, testing, code review and debugging.
Turn a user story into a clear, bounded task an agent can carry out: the goal, the constraints, the files and data involved, and how success will be checked.
Plan before generating: have the agent propose an approach, challenge it, and agree the design before code is written.
Verify everything an agent produces. Read the diff, run the tests, exercise the change in the running application, and reject work you cannot explain.
Own what you merge. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand, and you answer for it in review and in production.
Keep credentials, customer data and other sensitive information out of prompts and agent context, and follow PDI's AI usage policies.
Improve the team's shared setup: project instructions, reusable prompts and skills, test fixtures and other context that make agents more reliable for everyone.
Know when not to use an agent and recognize when one is going in circles or producing plausible but wrong output.
Required Skills & Experience:
Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field plus 4 to 6 years of experience building or maintaining software in a product development environment, or equivalent experience.
Working proficiency in C# and .NET (ASP.NET Core), including building and consuming REST APIs.
Working proficiency in a modern JavaScript framework with TypeScript; React is preferred.
Solid SQL skills on a relational database (SQL Server or PostgreSQL): queries, stored procedures and basic performance tuning.
Hands-on experience using coding agents or AI coding assistants in real project work, and the ability to show how you directed and verified their output.
Computer science fundamentals: object-oriented programming, design patterns, data structures and algorithms.
Practical experience with Git, pull requests, CI/CD pipelines and Agile delivery.
Habit of writing automated tests for your own code.
Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to explain technical concepts in non-technical terms. Clear writing matters more here than usual, because it is also how you direct agents.
Self-starter who can work independently as part of a distributed team, manage competing priorities and learn an unfamiliar codebase quickly.
Other Skills and Experience:
AWS experience: Lambda, SQS, S3, RDS, CloudWatch.
Experience building agent workflows: custom instructions, skills, MCP servers or agent-run test and review loops.
React Native or Expo mobile development.
Payments or subscription billing integrations, such as Stripe.
Retail, convenience store, point-of-sale or fuel domain experience.
Azure DevOps, Jenkins, Docker and infrastructure as code (OpenTofu or Terraform).
Monitoring and tracing with Datadog or a similar tool.
Experience maintaining or migrating a legacy .NET Framework application.
Behavioral Competencies:
Cultivates Innovation
Decision Quality
Manages Complexity
Drives Results
Business Insight
PDI is committed to offering a well-rounded benefits program, designed to support and care for you, and your family throughout your life and career. This includes a competitive salary, market-competitive benefits, and a quarterly perks program. We encourage a good work-life balance with ample time off [time away] and, where appropriate, hybrid working arrangements. Employees have access to continuous learning, professional certifications, and leadership development opportunities. Our global culture fosters diversity, inclusion, and values authenticity, trust, curiosity, and diversity of thought, ensuring a supportive environment for all.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. https://www.naukri.com/job-listings-full.text: Role Overview If you want to do serious engineering on hard Earth-science problems, this is the job. We're looking for a full-stack engineer, strongest on the backend, to take our data platform from working prototype to production, and keep it running. Responsibilities Because we pull together so many kinds of science, the data is scattered and sparse. Some of it is scanned maps from decades ago, and it arrives in about a dozen coordinate systems. Your job is to make it fast and get it right, so people can trust what they're looking at. In practice, you'll be:  Building the ingest workers that take files in, fix or flag their coordinate systems, convert them to GeoParquet, Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF or Zarr, and record where every version came from Keeping the store honest: immutable versions on S3, a catalogue that points at the current one, a review step before anything goes live, and rollback that's just a pointer move Getting data in front of people through the API, pre-built map tiles behind a CDN, and 3D views of subsurface models Writing the analysis workers that compute statistics from the original data, not a resampled copy, using DuckDB, xarray and rasterio Making sure licence and sensitivity rules hold everywhere data leaves the system And the unglamorous work that keeps all of us sane: CI on every push, infrastructure as code, monitoring, backups we've actually tried restoring, and secret scanning.  Requirements You've built backend systems, run them in production, and been the one who got called when they broke. Beyond that, we'd like to see most of these:  Four or more years of backend work that real users depended on Python you're very comfortable in, including async services and files too big to fit in memory MongoDB or another document store, plus solid SQL, and a feel for when data belongs in files rather than a database AWS in practice: S3, queues, containers and a CDN, ideally set up as infrastructure as code Enough JavaScript or TypeScript to ship a frontend feature on your own, maps included Good habits: you write tests, you care about CI and code review, and you write down why you decided something A liking for vague problems. You'd rather measure than guess, and you say plainly what you found  Nice to have  GDAL, PROJ, rasterio, GeoPandas or Shapely, and knowing why datums matter (vertical ones too) GeoParquet, Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF, Zarr or NetCDF, and STAC DuckDB's spatial extension, xarray or H3 Vector tiles, deck.gl or MapLibre, and 3D in the browser Time spent with geophysical grids, geochemistry, borehole logs, or satellite and hyperspectral imagery Work where lineage and reproducibility really mattered PostGIS  How we work We have a handful of operating principles. Three of them shape engineering more than the rest.  Building with Velocity. We move fast but for us that means less friction, not rushing. You'll own a lot and ship early: your first change should reach production within a few weeks, and you'll own whole services soon after. Kalaakari Kaarigari. We care about craft. A map that never quietly drops a small feature, a pipeline that explains why it rejected a file, an error a geologist can act on. "It works" is where we start, not where we stop. The Science Behind Everything. We write decisions down with the numbers behind them, and we don't call something fast until we've measured it. The people using what you build are geologists, geochemists and ML researchers, and they'll tell you quickly when something doesn't add up. Our numbers end up in front of auditors and partners, so we'd rather a page be slow than quietly wrong. Disclaimer: This job posting has been aggregated from external source. About Sycamore

Sycamore is building the trusted agent operating system for the enterprise. Our platform helps companies build, deploy, and orchestrate agentic apps that take on real operational work, with the security and control large organizations need.

We are a small, engineering-led team working directly with Fortune 500 enterprises. We have raised $65M from Coatue and Lightspeed, along with other investors and industry leaders.

The role

The simplest way to describe this role: you are the engineer in the customer room and the product engineer who ships what the room needs.

You will map how an important workflow works today, identify where an agent can create a measurable outcome, and build the application end to end. That can include the user experience, APIs and data model, agent instructions and tools, enterprise integrations, permissions, approval points, durable workflows, and the operational controls needed to run safely.

You own the full loop: discovery, implementation, realistic testing, preview and deployment, production debugging, adoption, and iteration. Your work does not end with a prototype, a requirements document, or a handoff.

Customer-specific product work belongs with you. When the same runtime, connector, memory, approval, or deployment need appears repeatedly, you work with Core AI or Infrastructure to turn it into a reusable capability instead of maintaining parallel custom implementations.

What the work looks like

In one week, you might:

Sit with a customer's operators and engineering team to map a manual process, its domain entities, edge cases, permissions, approval points, and success criteria.

Trace how the workflow connects to existing systems and determine which reads and writes an agent can perform safely.

Build a production application across the user interface, backend APIs, data model, agent behavior, tools, integrations, and human-review surfaces.

Exercise the real workflow in a browser, run backend and end-to-end tests, inspect traces and structured events, and fix failures before users encounter them.

Deploy a preview or development version, work through customer security and networking constraints, and stay close to usage after launch.

Separate the customer's specific business behavior from a reusable platform pattern, then contribute the shared primitive with the relevant Core AI or Infrastructure engineer.

What you will do

Turn ambiguous enterprise problems into clear technical designs, working software, and measurable outcomes.

Build product surfaces for agent conversations, tasks, progress, approvals, artifacts, and operational workflows.

Design APIs and relational data models that accurately represent the customer's domain and remain understandable as the product evolves.

Build agent instructions, tool interfaces, connector interactions, and durable workflow steps with explicit permission and failure behavior.

Navigate enterprise requirements around authentication, authorization, tenant isolation, data handling, deployment, observability, and change management.

Test realistic user journeys rather than stopping at isolated units or happy-path demos.

Debug across product code, agent behavior, integrations, infrastructure, and customer systems until the underlying failure is understood.

Stay accountable for reliability, adoption, and customer outcomes after launch.

Travel within India when working alongside users will accelerate discovery, delivery, or adoption.

The environment you will work in

Our current product environment includes TypeScript, React, TanStack, Tailwind, Python, FastAPI, typed data models, PostgreSQL, durable workflows, MCP-based tools and connectors, browser automation, and cloud-native deployment on Kubernetes.

We use automated tests, coding agents, traces, evaluations, and production feedback as part of everyday engineering.

This is context, not a checklist. We do not require previous experience with every language, framework, or vendor in our stack. Strong engineers who understand systems, learn quickly, and have shipped production software can become effective here without matching our tools one for one.

What we are looking for

5-12 years of software engineering experience. We will make exceptions for exceptional people in either direction.

Strong software fundamentals across product design, APIs, data modeling, distributed systems, testing, and production debugging.

Evidence that you personally shipped and operated meaningful software, rather than stopping at prototypes or delegating the production work.

Product judgment. You can find the real problem behind a request, choose a useful first version, and decide what should remain customer-specific versus become reusable.

Comfort moving across user interfaces, backend services, data, agent behavior, integrations, and deployment when the outcome requires it.

A security-minded approach to enterprise data, permissions, credentials, approvals, and auditability.

AI-native. You use coding agents and modern models as a force multiplier while still owning the architecture, understanding the code, and explaining important decisions.

Clear communication and high EQ. You can work with a customer's CTO, operators, security team, and engineers without losing technical depth.

Comfort with startup ambiguity, fast feedback loops, broad ownership, and regular customer travel.

Former founders, early product engineers, and forward-deployed engineers often do well in this role when they have retained real code and production ownership. That background is a signal, not a requirement.

What this role is not

It is not a pre-sales role that stops at a demo or architecture diagram.

It is not a solutions role that hands requirements to another engineering team.

It is not an ML research role focused on training foundation models.

It is not a narrow role defined by one programming language or layer of the stack.

It is not custom development without product judgment; repeated needs should improve the platform.

Interview process

A 30-minute introductory conversation.

Two 60-minute technical interviews, one focused on systems design and one on coding.

A take-home assignment where you build and present a real solution using the tools you would use on the job.

Why join

Work on AI systems that move from enterprise problems to production outcomes quickly.

Own the complete path from workflow discovery through adoption.

Shape both individual deployments and the product used across customers.

Join early enough to define how the India engineering team operates and grows.

Work as one engineering team across India and Palo Alto.

Receive competitive cash compensation and meaningful equity in the company you are helping build.

You co-own one Product.ai consumer surface end to end with the founder: the product strategy, the spec, the build, and the ship. Coding agents act as force multipliers. You own the verdict on whether it's right.

Product.ai is the verified truth layer for shopping: when a person or an AI agent needs to know what's actually true about a purchase, we answer with proof. SimplyCodes is the first proof at scale, the code verification service, at ~$22M a year in revenue. Profitable. Founder-owned since 2009, bootstrapped, no outside investors, no board. Fewer than twenty operators.

Why This Role Exists

Product.ai has more high-leverage consumer surfaces than owners. We're hiring product thinkers through several doors, and this is the engineer's door: someone who came up writing code, has shipped things people use, and now wants to co-own product strategy, user experience, and product outcomes end to end instead of working off a ticket queue.

Our consumer and monetization thesis is clear: on the consumer side, our Verification Checker lets any shopper paste what an AI, an article, a brand page, or a friend told them to buy, and we grade the claims inside it across five verification states — free to consumers to win trust and habit. On the monetization side, AI systems and shopping agents pay per call for keyed access to our verified commerce truth.

A product engineer here co-owns what to build and how we know it worked. You weigh the data, the user, and your own product taste, make the calls in the gray area, write the spec, and direct coding agents as force multipliers alongside your own hands-on code. You take end-to-end ownership of a major consumer surface — from the Verification Checker's interactive consumer loop and preference-aware personalization to the consumer experience inside ChatGPT, Apple App Intents, Gemini, and Claude — partnering directly with the founder and our Founding Designer.

The System You'll Need to Model
The Verification Checker and decision-shaped consumer interfaces. Shoppers paste any recommendation — from an AI, an article, a brand page, or a friend — and the Verification Checker grades the claims inside it across five verification states with citations intact, including when the honest answer is "don't buy." The user changes a constraint and watches the verdict move. Streaming, citation-bearing, trust-critical: one wrong claim rendered confidently costs more than a month of speed.
Agent-First Commerce and products inside AI platforms. While the consumer Verification Checker stays free to win trust, AI shopping agents pay per call for keyed access to our verified commerce truth, and millions of shoppers encounter our verdicts inside ChatGPT, Apple App Intents, Gemini, or Claude. You own what a person sees and does once a verdict arrives.
Preference-aware answers. A verdict that remembers what this shopper cares about across our Preference Graph, Truth Graph, and Commerce Graph is a different product from one that doesn't. It's a data model, a consent and trust problem, and an interface problem at once, designed together.
A spec-driven agentic build pipeline. Intent becomes a visual mockup, then a locked spec, then coding agents build as force multipliers, and separate verifier agents grade the build against the spec. Your product judgment, code craft, and spec precision gate what ships.
Several surfaces, one system. Web (/shop and SimplyCodes), browser extension, assistant platforms, and the /shop Design Record that spans them: different interaction contracts, one truth backend, one shared component architecture.
Cortex, the shared AI brain the company runs on. You work inside it daily, directing coding agents the way our founder does, and since August any operator here can change the rules the company runs on, live, without waiting on founder approval.

If reading that energizes you, keep going. If it feels overwhelming or underspecified, this isn't the right fit.

What You Will Own

One consumer surface and its strategy, end to end. Co-owning the product strategy, user experience, metrics, roadmap, and production code the way a technical founder owns a product. Your surface carries falsifiable outcomes, each with an evidence test a stranger could run.

The product calls in the gray area. When does a five-state verification indicator build trust, and when does it add friction? When is "don't buy this" the right thing to render boldly? You weigh the data, the user, and your taste, and you decide alongside the founder and our Founding Designer.

The spec, the components, and the ship gate. Partnering directly with our Founding Designer on the /shop Design Record, you take features from interactive prototype and locked spec to shipped production code in TypeScript and React.

Verification for agent-written product code. You define what "correct" means for a streaming, citation-bearing interface and make that definition executable: verifier agents, evaluation suites for interface behavior, and gates that catch drift before a shopper sees it.

Your seat charter. Within your first quarter you co-sign a charter for this seat. It names one machine-checkable number that proves the seat is working, and a high-ownership partnership model with the founder.

The craft you must already own: shipping consumer product to real users in TypeScript and React, and making product strategy calls you can defend. Comparable experience we accept: senior full-stack or frontend work with real product ownership, a founding engineer seat at a consumer company, or a product you built and shipped on your own. What you'll grow into here: directing coding agents as force multipliers, evaluation design for interfaces, and distribution across AI assistants.

Who You Are

How you think. You form a working model of a system — a truth backend, a multi-surface frontend, an agent loop — and you notice fast when the model is wrong and update without ego. You don't wait for scope to be handed to you; enough signal and first principles get you moving.

How you work. You move between product strategy and shipped code without getting stuck at either altitude: a user problem in the morning becomes a prototype by noon and a verified change in production by evening. You treat coding agents as force multipliers you verify because you can do the whole job by hand.

What you've probably built. Consumer products with real users, where you can point to the product calls you made and what happened after: a streaming interface, a design system, an evaluation harness for AI output, an agent workflow you built because you needed it. Adjacent roads count: platform apps, browser extensions, developer tools with a consumer edge. We care about the artifact and the reasoning more than where you did it.

Who this isn't for. This is wrong if you wait for a ticket or spec to start; here you co-own the strategy and write the spec. It's wrong if you want a narrow lane; a consumer surface is product judgment, design collaboration, engineering, and verification in one seat. And it's wrong if your code is whatever a model handed you without knowing why it's right. You'll be happiest here if you want the whole problem and want to be measured on what your surface does for the people using it.

How We Hire

We don't run traditional engineering interviews.

Async video screen (4-minute Builder Pulse). Three short questions (about 4 minutes total, starting with your most exceptional achievement), on your own time, replacing the recruiter screen, alongside links to any standout GitHub profile or live shipped consumer products on your application.
Calls with company stakeholders. Short conversations with the people you'd build beside.
Conversation with the founder. Product taste, how you model the Verification Checker and the systems above, and how you reason in the gray area.
Paid work trial (PRJ-76 / PRJ-77). A paid $5,000 two-week sprint in our environment, shipping production TypeScript/React code and product specs on a live consumer surface. We look for product taste, engineering rigor, how you use coding agents as force multipliers, and how we collaborate together.

If the work above reads like yours but your resume is unconventional, apply anyway. We hire on the work and the reasoning, not the pedigree.

Compensation & Ownership

Base salary: $185,000 – $225,000 (W-2 cash base; typical starting offers enter in the $185K–$205K half, with upper-band placement for proven end-to-end consumer surface ownership).

Product.ai is a profitable, founder-owned company generating ~$22M/yr in revenue with zero venture debt. Eligible for the company's performance-based ownership and annual profit-share programs, plus 100% company-paid health coverage for you and your family; ownership mechanics and grant terms are discussed at the offer stage. Unlimited AI token budget steered by return.

Based in Santa Monica, Los Angeles, on our high-trust hybrid rhythm: four focused in-office half-days together (Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday from 9am to 2pm), with Wednesdays open for deep work and afternoons yours to work from wherever you do your best work. Relocation support available for the right builder.
